The head of the GOP’s Senate campaign arm was questioned in a new interview about why recent ads sponsored by Senate Republicans were highlighting Abdul El-Sayed’s full name — Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed — instead of the name he uses personally.

Sen. Tim Scott appeared on a pre-taped interview with Manu Raju on CNN’s State of the Union Sunday to discuss the upcoming midterm cycle, where his party is defending twin congressional majorities against strong traditional headwinds facing the president’s party as well as the striking unpopularity of the current occupant of the White House.

Scott was asked directly by Raju if the purpose of ads highlighting a name El-Sayed has never used in public was an intentional reference to his Arab-American heritage and Muslim faith. Scott denied this, but couldn’t explain why the National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) was backing such ads, or offer any alternative purpose for using El-Sayed’s extended full name.

Instead, Scott pivoted twice to claiming that the former Wayne County public health director was “dangerous”.

“Why not just use the name he goes by?” Raju asked Scott, who responded: “Listen, I go by Timothy Eugene. People call me that all the time.”

open image in gallery Tim Scott leads the Senate Republican campaign arm, the NRSC ( AFP/Getty )

“It’s about what he stands for,” insisted Scott. “We’re going to focus and bring attention to the fact that not only is he sympathetic to Hamas, not only does he run around with Hasan Piker, someone who said ‘America deserves 9/11’, he should be held to account for exactly where he stands, and what he’s for.”

El-Sayed separately responded to the controversy on the same program during an interview with Jake Tapper as he was asked about Donald Trump’s social media post showing him in a diner booth with his wife, who wears a hijab, and contrasting the image to a picture of Trump and his wife Melania.

Democrats, supporters of El-Sayed, and independent observers of the race have all argued that the combined Republican effort is aimed at highlighting El-Sayed’s Muslim faith and background with obviously bigoted undertones.

open image in gallery Abdul El-Sayed compared Republicans' attempts to highlight his name to similar tactics used against Barack Obama ( Reuters )

Responding to Tapper, El-Sayed declined to get into a discussion about his faith or background and instead pivoted to a snarky comment about rumored marital troubles and personal animosity between Trump and his wife Melania, who is rarely spotted at the White House amid his second term.

But on NBC’s Meet the Press, he was more explicit with his description of the Republican attack lines: "Notice how they chose to use my full name, in echoes to exactly what they did against President Obama.”

El-Sayed told NBC and CNN that he’d spoken with former President Barack Obama since the primary and has invoked Obama’s middle name, Hussein, and Obama’s 2008 candidacy as spurring his own belief that someone with an Arabic name could succeed in American politics despite anti-Muslim bigotry. Obama’s 2008 campaign was subject to such bigotry openly, and Republicans for years described him, falsely and wholly without evidence, of secretly adhering to the Muslim faith. In one famous moment, his opponent John McCain admonished his own supporter onstage for echoing such attacks.

open image in gallery Barack Obama has not made his endorsement in the Michigan Senate race but recently spoke with El-Sayed, according to the candidate ( AP )

Supporters of the progressive candidate, who narrowly won Michigan’s Senate primary last week, labeled the attacks he faced during the primary at the hands of AIPAC and other organizations associated with the pro-Israel lobby grossly Islamophobic and in many cases rooted in clear misinformation. AIPAC and its allies vowed in a statement after El-Sayed’s victory to continue attacking him ahead of the general election in November, when he will face the Trump-endorsed Mike Rogers.

El-Sayed’s association with Piker, who attended his election night watch party and campaigned with him on several occasions, has also contributed to the controversies surrounding his campaign. His opponents, including Scott and Republicans, label Piker an anti-Semite and left-wing radical with a history of statements about America and foreign policy that are often highly critical of both U.S. interests and Israel. Piker’s supporters, however, view the criticism as part of a smear campaign.

In his interview with NBC on Sunday, El-Sayed refused to disavow Piker and hit out at members of the media and his own party for engaging in “cancel culture.”

“I want to be held accountable for what I say and do, rather than this idea that we’ve, we’re so stuck in cancel culture that we all agreed was a bad idea back in 2020 but we seem to want to bring back,” said El-Sayed.

Piker himself noted on a stream Friday that he was “tired” of apologizing for the comment, something he said he’d done repeatedly to total disinterest from his critics.

British retail bosses report a big surge in demand for physical collectibles among young people, with squishy dumplings, trading cards, and K-Pop CDs proving particularly popular.

One chain said that it is selling thousands of squishies every week, as retailers tap into popular culture to drive sales among children and young adults.

Music and entertainment retailer HMV, which operates 114 stores across the UK, has seen a 12 per cent increase in visitor numbers during the first half of this year compared to the same period in 2025.

The trajectory suggests about 50 million store visits are anticipated over the course of this year.

The growth is largely attributed to post-pandemic efforts to revitalise store spaces.

That includes creating dedicated zones for pop culture merchandise, including soft squishy toys, trading cards, and K-pop items.

open image in gallery Squishy dumpling toys are popular with children ( Getty Images )

HMV’s managing director Phil Halliday said: “For years, it was quiet on a Saturday, and that’s when the kids used to come in.

“The store colleagues will tell you, it’s heaving on a Saturday now… and you can see it in the numbers.

“Kids are coming back in because they want to be around each other and spaces where they can gather to share experiences… not everyone wants to sit at home on the computer,” he said.

High street chain The Works also said it was getting a boost from children coming into shops with pocket money to spend.

The retailer has more than 500 shops in the UK and Ireland and sells items including books, toys and games, arts and crafts, and stationery.

It said that squishies had surged in popularity since May and it was selling thousands a week – including the “mini dumplings”, which can be calming for children to squeeze in their hands as well as becoming an item to collect and trade.

open image in gallery Pokemon cards are also popular with young people ( AFP/Getty )

The Works also highlighted sales growth for products like Pokemon cards, children’s colouring and puzzle books, crafts and art supplies.

The company has taken a punt on a “screen-free” strategy after noticing increased demand from parents looking for activities to reduce their children’s screen time, according to chief executive Gavin Peck.

He said: “We’ve seen a lot more people, even adults, taking up art, thinking ‘I want to try colouring books or I want to try crafting to ease my mind’.

“We’ve seen real demand coming from customers.”

The government has announced plans to ban social media for under-16s, which could be in place by spring 2027.

Mr Peck said: “If the government gets behind something it certainly heightens the overall screen-free message and therefore we’re there to support those customers that are looking for screen-free alternatives, so it can only have a positive impact on us.”

Meanwhile, Mr Halliday said that popular musicians like Olivia Rodrigo, Ariane Grande, Olivia Dean and BTS were also driving a resurgence in demand for music in physical formats, despite access to streaming.

This has translated into stronger trading for HMV, with vinyl sales up 27 per cent in stores and 45 per cent online year-on-year, while CD sales have jumped by a 10th.

open image in gallery BTS are among the artists driving a surge in sales of physical CDs ( Reuters )

Interest in CDs has been led in part by young people buying K-pop albums.

“A lot of that product is on CD,” Mr Halliday said, adding: “We’ve definitely doubled down on it and tried to really improve the offer. And kids are seeing it as a more cost-effective alternative to vinyl.”

“There is an entire depth of experience and connection with these products that you don’t get from streaming,” he said, also pointing to sustained demand for DVDs.

“There is definitely a sentiment shift towards physical ownership.”

The appeal of collecting “retro” technology among younger people has extended to devices, with eBay pointing to a surge in the number of searches and prices of the iPhone 5C – which was introduced by Apple in 2013.

The company said searches increased by 164 per cent globally in the year to January 2026 while the average sales price increased by 55 per cent in the UK.

Andy Burnham faces pressure over North Sea oil and gas as a decision on allowing new drilling moves closer.

As Britain braces for its fifth heatwave, environmental groups have urged the Prime Minister to refuse permission for oil and gas production in two areas of the North Sea, known as Jackdaw and Rosebank, as part of the fight against climate change.

But opposition politicians, the oil and gas industry and US President Donald Trump have called for him to grant permission, arguing this would protect jobs and cut household bills.

Mr Burnham’s party is also split on the issue, while watering down environmental commitments could limit Labour’s ability to tempt back voters that have switched to the Greens since 2024.

open image in gallery Climate activists say the Rosebank and Jackdaw projects would ‘further fuel climate chaos’ (PA) ( PA Archive )

Production at both Jackdaw and Rosebank was approved by the Conservatives, but a court quashed those decisions last year after a challenge from Greenpeace, leaving the Labour Government to decide whether to go ahead.

On Monday, a further consultation on Jackdaw, a gas field 150 miles east of Aberdeen will close, while a consultation on the Rosebank oil field, north-west of Shetland, closes a week later.

The end of the consultations has brought renewed focus on the Prime Minister’s dilemma.

Lang Banks, director of WWF Scotland, said there was “a clear choice to be made by our politicians: further fuel climate chaos, or support a fair transition to a safer future”.

Pointing to “a summer of extreme heat and devastating wildfires”, including near Aberdeen, Mr Banks said it would be “irresponsible to approve new oil and gas developments that would accelerate climate change and do nothing to lower the energy bills of UK households”.

open image in gallery (PA Graphics) ( PA Graphics )

Other environmental groups have argued that the small amount of oil and gas left in Britain’s North Sea holdings would make little difference to either prices, which are set internationally, or energy security, while increasing carbon emissions.

Ami McCarthy, head of politics at Greenpeace UK, said: “Trying to squeeze the last few drops of expensive oil and gas out of the North Sea while the world is reeling from climate impacts is beyond ridiculous.

“The Government should hold fast on their no new oil and gas commitment. We need true investment in the clean energy industries of the future, which are our only dependable path to good jobs, lower bills, and long-term prosperity.”

But supporters of further drilling, including the energy industry, the Conservatives and some trade unions, say it will not make a significant difference to emissions and is vital for protecting jobs.

Mr Trump has also been a vocal supporter of North Sea drilling, and said Mr Burnham “sounded terrific” on the issue in their first phone call last month.

In that call, Mr Burnham told Mr Trump the UK “can’t ignore” resources in the North Sea, and said he would take “a pragmatic approach” to further drilling.

But the Prime Minister could face an internal battle if he does approve production at Jackdaw and Rosebank.

Some within Labour back the move. Scottish MP Graeme Downie said the UK should “manage the decline of the North Sea in a way that protects workers, supports communities and builds the industries that will power Britain’s future”.

He added: “If we do not proceed with Jackdaw and Rosebank, investment will leave the UK, jobs will disappear and expertise will be lost.

“We also risk shattering the foundations of our industry and destroying the very skills we need to deliver a low-carbon future for the UK and lead the world on new technology and expertise.”

But others have warned against granting permission, pointing to Labour’s 2024 manifesto commitment not to grant new licences for drilling in the North Sea.

Labour has always said it would honour existing licences, giving it some room to approve production at Jackdaw and Rosebank.

But Norwich South MP Clive Lewis said it was a “clear commitment” and allowing production at the two fields would be “a major step backwards”.

In a letter to new Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh, Mr Lewis said: “Analysts have said that the May and June 2026 heatwaves were associated with more than 2,700 excess heat-related deaths across England and Wales.

“These events are becoming more frequent and severe as climate breakdown intensifies, driven largely by greenhouse gas emissions from the burning of fossil fuels, including oil and gas.

“Against this background, approving new drilling would undermine efforts to address the climate crisis and put a safe, liveable future further out of reach.”

open image in gallery

Meanwhile, polling suggests Labour under Mr Burnham has begun to win back some of the voters it lost to the Greens during Sir Keir Starmer’s premiership, but this could be jeopardised if the party was seen to water down its climate commitments.

Green leader Zack Polanski said approving Jackdaw and Rosebank would be “a dereliction of duty”.

He said: “Whatever weasel words are used on drilling within new or existing licences, one of the new Prime Minister’s first significant decisions would be to break Labour’s manifesto pledge.

“Jackdaw’s owner have themselves said that only 27 direct full time jobs would be created if given the go ahead.

“This has nothing to do with boosting the economy for the people of this country and far more to do with boosting obscene profits for fossil fuel companies and their shareholders.

“I made clear in my press conference last week, this needs to be treated for the serious crisis it is, with financial support for homes to keep cool and for fossil fuel giants to pay the costs of extreme weather adaptation.”

A Government spokesperson said: “The North Sea remains a vital national asset, supporting jobs, growth and the UK’s energy security.

“We are clear that oil and gas will continue to play an important role in our energy system for decades to come, alongside renewables, nuclear and other low-carbon technologies.

“Our focus is on providing stability and supporting North Sea workers and communities as they continue to make a vital contribution to the UK’s economy.”

It has been revealed that cameras on Royal Navy drones were connected to a system in China, prompting security concerns despite the Ministry of Defence insisting no sensitive data was compromised.

The Daily Telegraph reported that cameras on the Navy’s K3 Scout surveillance drone were found to be sending so-called "heartbeat communications" to a device in the country.

The information exchanged reportedly only included confirmation that the camera was online and functioning normally. However, the breach is expected to spark wider concern about the security of military drone components.

A Ministry of Defence spokesperson stated the transmissions had been identified during a "routine cyber vulnerability assessment" of the K3 drones.

open image in gallery A Ministry of Defence spokesperson stated the transmissions had been identified during a ‘routine cyber vulnerability assessment’ of the K3 drones ( UK MOD/Crown copyright )

They added: “A thorough investigation found no evidence of MoD data or systems being accessed, compromised or transmitted externally.

“Our assurance and testing processes are designed to identify and address potential vulnerabilities early, and we continue to undertake routine security activity across our systems and equipment.”

The K3 Scout is produced by Kraken Technology Group, a British company based in Fareham, Hampshire, but the cameras are understood to have been provided by a third party that gave assurances about their security.

The Royal Navy has bought 20 of the K3s as part of its drone project, Operation Beehive.

The uncrewed vessels are expected to perform a range of tasks including surveillance, force protection and precision strike roles as the Navy moves to a “hybrid” model that incorporates more drones.

In May, the MoD announced that the drones would form part of a potential deployment to protect shipping in the Strait of Hormuz in the event of a lasting ceasefire in the region. The UK announced it would deploy autonomous mine-hunting equipment, “cutting-edge” anti-drone systems and Typhoon jets as part of its mission in the Strait of Hormuz, John Healey said.

The package included autonomous mine-hunting technology capable of deploying high-speed Kraken drone boats, as well as Typhoon jets for air patrols. The UK had already announced the deployment of HMS Dragon to the region, allowing the destroyer to support the multinational mission if conditions allowed.

Mr Healey said: “With our allies, this multinational mission will be defensive, independent, and credible.”

Hall of Famer Don Nelson, the second-winningest coach in NBA history, has died at the age of 86. His family announced the passing of the five-time champion as a player on Sunday, though they did not disclose the manner of death.

"On Sunday morning our beloved husband, dad, grandfather and great-grandfather Don Nelson peacefully went to be with the Lord, surrounded by his loving family," the Nelson family statement read. "Throughout his last week, friends and family encircled him with love, sharing the blessing of his friendship and revisiting treasured memories."

Nelson retired in 2010 as the all-time leader with 1,335 regular-season coaching victories, a record later surpassed by San Antonio Spurs coach Gregg Popovich (1,390). His distinctive fast-paced style, utilizing smaller athletic players, became famously known as "Nellie Ball."

open image in gallery Nelson retired in 2010 as the all-time leader with 1,335 regular-season coaching victories ( Jim Rogash/Getty Images )

The three-time Coach of the Year didn't win any NBA titles during his 31-year overall tenure with the Milwaukee Bucks (1976-87), Golden State Warriors (1988-95, 2006-10), New York Knicks (1995-96) and Dallas Mavericks (1997-2005). But he put together 13 seasons of 50 or more wins, twice reaching 60 (once with the Bucks, once with the Mavericks).

"[Nelson] was a true basketball visionary who saw the game differently and was never afraid to challenge conventional thinking," the Warriors said in a statement. "His approach helped shape the game and paved the way for generations of players and coaches who followed.

"More than anything, Don Nelson will be remembered for his authenticity, larger-than-life personality, and incredible passion for basketball, and his influence on the Warriors franchise will endure for years to come."

He was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame as a coach in 2012.

As a player, Nelson won five NBA titles during 11 seasons with the Boston Celtics.

He initially reached the NBA with the Chicago Zephyrs (1962-63) after being the No. 3 overall pick. He then spent two seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers before joining behind a loaded Boston starting five and was one of seven Boston players to average double digits in scoring in 1967-68. He averaged a career best 15.4 points and 7.3 rebounds in 1969-70.

In 134 career playoff games, Nelson averaged 11.1 points and 4.8 rebounds. The Celtics retired his No. 19 jersey in 1978.

"Don Nelson revolutionized NBA basketball through his fearlessness, ingenuity and deep conviction," NBA commissioner Adam Silver said in a statement. "He spent nearly 50 years in the NBA - winning five championships as a player with the Boston Celtics before building one of the most successful and pioneering coaching careers in league history. He brought an unmistakable personality to everything he did, and his impact on our sport will continue to be felt for generations.

"I send my deepest condolences to Don's family and many friends throughout our league."

In college, Nelson averaged 21.1 points and 10.9 rebounds in 72 games over three seasons at Iowa.

Nelson won the 2025 Chuck Daly Lifetime Achievement Award to honor his overall contributions to basketball.

The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. A newly released Food and Drug Administration report details the full scope of a massive produce recall connected to a nationwide cyclospora outbreak, naming major restaurant chains and retail brands that pulled nearly 240,000 cases of lettuce.

Saturday’s update identifies potential cyclospora contamination as the cause for the July 2026 recall initiated by supplier Taylor Farms.

In total, 236,192 cases of iceberg and romaine lettuce — some mixed with carrots and red cabbage — were removed from distribution across Mexico and 27 U.S. states.

Walmart’s house brand Marketside received the largest share of the recalled produce, accounting for 109,476 cases of salad and shredded lettuce.

Fast-food chains were also heavily affected. Subway removed 8,075 cases, Yum! Brands — the parent company of Taco Bell, KFC and Pizza Hut — recalled 5,900 cases, and Jack in the Box removed 5,130 cases. While Yum! Brands operates multiple companies, only Taco Bell has been tied to the recall so far.

open image in gallery A newly published FDA report reveals the scale of a major produce recall tied to a national cyclospora outbreak, listing the top grocery brands and fast-food chains that removed almost 240,000 cases of lettuce from distribution ( AP )

Other commercial accounts listed in the federal report include major food distributors Sysco, Markon, Peak Lettuce Salad and US Foods subsidiary Cross Valley Farms.

The disclosure comes after nonprofit consumer advocacy group Consumer Federation of America criticized Taylor Farms on July 21 for using obscure shorthand abbreviations on recall notices, such as “MKTSD” for Marketside and “CV” for Cross Valley Farms.

The recalled produce was sourced from central Mexico and distributed across a wide geographic footprint, including Florida, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Texas and Virginia.

The report offers the clearest picture yet of a health crisis that escalated over the summer.

As reported by The Independent, federal health officials have tracked more than 22,700 cyclospora cases nationwide, leading to more than 500 hospitalizations and two deaths.

The microscopic parasite, which is transmitted through exposure to human fecal matter, causes severe gastrointestinal illness, explosive diarrhea and dehydration.

open image in gallery Federal health officials have linked the parasite outbreak to more than 22,000 illnesses and 500 hospitalizations nationwide, with Michigan hit hardest ( Wiki Commons )

Michigan has been as the epicenter of the crisis, accounting for more than 12,000 reported cases.

However, state health officials recently advised residents that they could resume eating bagged salads, noting that new case reports and emergency room visits were slowing down and that contaminated produce from the early summer harvest wa no longer in circulation.

In an interview with CBS Face the Nation on Sunday, National Institutes of Health Director Jay Bhattacharya defended the Trump administration’s response to the outbreak, hailing FDA officials who did a “great job” trying to identify the source.

The outbreak has also taken a toll on the restaurant industry. Taco Bell reported a sales decline of roughly 2 percent during its recent fiscal quarter.

“The brand has seen a meaningful near-term sales impact,” Yum! Brands CEO Chris Turner told analysts on a recent earnings call, according to CNBC.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want
News.content:
Liverpool 2 Monaco 3

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho reveals he agreed to REPLACE Fergie at Man Utd before tearful phone call saw Special One return to Chelsea
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO has sensationally revealed he had agreed to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United manager.

But the Portuguese boss pulled out of the deal at the last minute and rang Sir Alex in tears to tell him the news.



Mourinho, 63, has opened up on the dramatic tale from 2013 during his new self-titled documentary that will premier on Netflix tomorrow.

And the Special One has explained how his “love” for Chelsea made him return to Stamford Bridge, when he could have got the United job ahead of David Moyes.



Speaking in his new doc, Mourinho said: “I go to Chelsea in 2013, but in that period there is something that nobody knows.

“I think I can say because I don’t hurt anyone with the truth and I think the objective of this work we are doing is to tell the truth.



“When I left Real Madrid, I signed with Manchester United to go to Manchester United after Sir Alex.

“I was, of course, very flattered, because Man United has an incredible appeal.

“When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Man United is very, very close.

“But one thing is love for football and another thing is love for a certain club. I think this is more powerful than love for football.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“And, fundamentally, after Real Madrid, I needed to feel that I am loved.

“For me to lose the chance to be the coach that succeeded Sir Alex Ferguson was dramatic.

“But I don’t regret it, because it was a decision that I made with my heart.

“And I think it is nature that says that when you do something for love, you are never doing anything wrong. I think it is nature. I did it for love.”



Sir Alex was convinced that Mourinho would be following in his footsteps after the pair held talks.

The Special One was coming off the back of a turbulent three years at Real Madrid where he had fallen out with the dressing room.

Mourinho did, however, win LaLiga during his second season and beat Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona to the Copa del Rey the year before.

The Real Madrid boss eventually took charge of United in 2016, three years after Sir Alex thought he would be the man to directly succeed him.



Sir Alex said in the documentary: “He was offered the job, yes. I sat him down and explained the situation.

“And, as far as I was concerned, he was accepting. And then, within hours, it changed.

“Early evening, he phoned me and he was crying.

“And he says, ‘Alex, I cannot take it, I gave my word to Chelsea and I am not going to break my word.’

“The reason he gave to me I can understand, but I was disappointed.”

Sports.title: John Terry admits Jose Mourinho’s Chelsea once obtained training footage of Sam Allardyce’s BOLTON to boost title bid
Sports.content:
CHELSEA once obtained footage of Bolton training to help their Premier League title challenge.

Long before Southampton were caught out spying on Middlesbrough ahead of last season’s Championship play-offs, Jose Mourinho’s Blues were up to tricks of their own.



An interesting revelation from the new Netflix documentary is Mourinho’s use of video analysis.

Andre Villas-Boas, who would later go on to manage Chelsea and Tottenham, was in charge of that area.



AVB said: “That was the breakthrough in terms of match analysis. Not a lot of people were doing it to the extent that we were doing it at the time.

“It was the old times of the DVD players and sometimes the DVD player didn’t work, and Jose used to destroy the projector or the DVD player!”

One of the video sessions involved footage from Sam Allardyce’s Bolton training session ahead of Chelsea playing them.

Captain John Terry explained: “Big Sam is saying: ‘Hit Gallas, he’s not very good in the air’. He’s spitting and stuff like that on the mic.

“And it was just like – wow, who gets footage from someone’s training ground? I am actually still not sure where he got the footage from!”

Terry says he would have been prepared to be carried out in a “coffin” for former boss Mourinho.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The pair spent five-and-a-half seasons together across two spells in a trophy-ladden period for Chelsea, winning three Premier League titles, three League Cups and one FA Cup.

Terry recounts being ignored in the treatment room by the Portuguese because he was injured.

The defender’s response was to take an injection for the pain so that he could join training. The physio argued he was “mad”.

But Terry said: “For him, I would give everything. I would leave that pitch in a coffin for him.”



There was – Terry insists – a “soft side” to Mourinho and every Sunday players were told to bring their kids to the training ground.

The Special One would crack jokes with them and showcase a part of his personality many did not see.

Even with an influx of big names, the core of Mourinho’s Chelsea during his first spell were England duo Terry and Frank Lampard.

They were his lieutenants in the dressing room and former skipper Terry vividly recalls the mood among the squad.

Mourinho described the players like “an army going into battle”.



Terry said: “There was a picture of the Premier League up in the dressing room.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“And there was a very clear mindset of: this is what we are going to win.

“From those first team meetings, to the very first game against Man United, the words and the terminology he would use in those meetings…like: ‘We are going to f*** them. We are going to win the league. We are going to take the trophy off them this year’.”

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho in pop at Pep Guardiola as Special One vows to NEVER take sabbatical and could manage into his SEVENTIES
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO cannot imagine retiring and believes he could still be managing in his 70s.

And the Special One has had a pop at his old rival Pep Guardiola by ruling out ever taking a sabbatical.



Mourinho, 63, returned to Real Madrid this summer for a second spell and signed a three-year contract.

But the Portuguese has revealed in his new Netflix documentary, Mourinho, that he has plenty of fuel in the tank.



Speaking in the doc, Mourinho said: “I cannot even imagine when I am going to stop my life in football.

“I say 10 more years, but maybe more than 10. It’s fun. It was, it is and will always be fun.



“I want to win more titles. I want to win new titles. I want to repeat titles.

“I want to do it in places where I have never been. I want to do it in places where I did before.

“My world is to walk in a football stadium with 50,000 or 90,000 [fans]. I had 100,000. That is my world.

“Without football, there is not something complete in me.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“But I don’t think it is an obsession. I don’t feel it as an obsession.

“It is just when you reach a certain level, you want to stay there forever.”

Mourinho has been in management since 2000, when he was placed in charge of Benfica.

The Special One’s new doc charts his rise from there, including a fiery three years at Real Madrid from 2010 to 2013.



Mourinho repeatedly clashed with Guardiola, who was managing Barcelona, during that period.

Pep ended up taking a break from football after leaving Barca in 2012 and took up the reins at Bayern Munich a year later.

But Mourinho has vowed he will never do the same, as taking time out from coaching would be a sign of weakness.

He said: “Some guys, they need a sabbatical – which is something that I hate. I hate that word.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“For me, sabbatical means weakness. Don’t speak with me about sabbaticals.



“I never need a rest. I will have a rest when he (Mourinho points to the sky) decides to say: ‘Come up’.”

Sports.title: England ace Eberechi Eze launches plans to build 30 new homes – but locals aren’t happy
Sports.content:
THREE Lions hero Eberechi Eze has launched ambitious plans to build 30 new homes as he climbs up the Premier League property ladder.

The Arsenal midfielder has become a director of two companies set up to oversee the project on the edge of the West Sussex village of Horsted Keynes.



It comes after the 28-year-old won the league with Arsenal and helped England claim third place at this summer’s World Cup.

A source said: “Rather than simply investing in buy-to-let properties like many footballers, Eze has entered the far more ambitious world of residential development, taking control of a site with planning permission already in place.



“Football might be paying the bills today, but developments like this can end up making players wealthier than their careers ever did.”

Companies House records show Eze has established EZE10 Residential (Horsted Keynes) Limited and become a director of Macar Homes (Horsted Keynes) Limited alongside Surrey developer Alex MacDonald and his wife Rachael.

The site already has permission for 30 homes, ranging from one-bedroom flats to four-bedroom houses, including nine affordable properties.

But the scheme attracted more than 260 objections, with residents raising concerns over traffic, road safety, over-development and the loss of greenfield land.

Campaigners also warned it would mean felling mature trees and harm the character of the historic Sussex village.

Despite the objections, council planners concluded the benefits outweighed the concerns and granted permission.



The project marks one of the most ambitious property ventures undertaken by a current England international, following footballers including Robbie Fowler, Gary Neville and John Terry into property investment.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Gabriel Martinelli ‘lined up for shock transfer to European giant after entering final year of contract’
Sports.content:
GABRIEL MARTINELLI could be on his way out of Arsenal this summer, according to reports.

The winger lost his place in the Gunners’ first team to Leandro Trossard last season, while Greek winger Christos Tzolis was signed this summer in a £34million deal from Club Brugge.



It has been widely expected Martinelli, 25, would depart for pastures new this summer, even after Trossard’s own exit to Turkish giants Besiktas.

But Martinelli could be set to follow the Belgian to the Turkish Super Lig.



That’s because, according to talkSPORT, reigning league champions Galatasaray have made an enquiry over his availability.

Galatasaray had been in talks to sign AC Milan outcast Rafael Leao and had earmarked Martinelli as an alternative option.

And they have now made contact with Arsenal over Martinelli’s status after failing to engineer a breakthrough in the Leao talks.

SunSport reported earlier in the window that if Martinelli was sold, he would be expected to depart for higher than the club’s current sale record of £35m paid by Liverpool for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain in 2017.

Whether Galatasaray are willing to stump up that sort of money remains to be seen, but it’s understood Arsenal will only sanction an exit for Martinelli if they can find a replacement.

The North London club had been in talks to sign Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr, but saw that deal collapse when the Brazilian signed a new deal through to 2032.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

However, SunSport looked at six alternative targets Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta could eye this window.

Among them were Paris Saint-Germain and France winger, Bradley Barcola – wanted by Liverpool but rated at £145m by his club – as well as Manchester United and England forward Marcus Rashford, and Athletic Bilbao and Spanish World Cup winner Nico Williams.

But reports have also suggested that Juventus‘ Kenan Yildiz, Atletico Madrid‘s Julian Alvarez, Everton‘s Iliman Ndiaye and Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi are all on their radar too.

A move for the latter star in that quartet seems very unlikely this summer given he is expected to miss at least four months following foot surgery he had at the end of July.

Sports.title: Embattled Gianni Infantino dealt fresh humiliation as local Swiss club snubs chance to back him
Sports.content:
SHAMED footie fatcat Gianni Infantino’s local club have refused to back his leadership of Fifa.

Zug 94, based in the luxury Swiss lakeside town where the embattled £4.8million-a-year chief has a penthouse flat, declined to endorse him.



It comes as Europe’s football governing body, Uefa, considers launching an investigation into his 16-year career there.

Infantino yesterday denied claims made by The Daily Telegraph that Uefa paid off an alleged mistress while he was the organisation’s general secretary.



A Fifa spokesman said he “strongly denies the allegations, and they are categorically untrue”.

It called the allegations part of a “concerted effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president”.



Uefa confirmed a departure payment had been made to the unnamed woman, whose salary was said to have been raised at married father Infantino’s request.

Infantino could be challenged in next March’s Fifa presidential election after Football Associations of several nations, including England and Wales, withdrew their endorsements.

Zug 94, who play in the Swiss fourth division and have an average attendance of 400, also dodged offering its backing.

When asked by The Sun if Zug 94 supported Infantino’s continued leadership, a club spokesman said: “We will refrain from commenting on this matter.”



Infantino switched his tax residency from Zurich to Zug in 2022.

He has a £6,500-a-month penthouse apartment overlooking Lake Zug in the Swiss tax haven.

Fifa pays his rent.

Sports.title: WAGs should be offered counselling by clubs because of struggles with trolls, other women & their partners, study finds
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL clubs should offer counselling to the wives and girlfriends of players, the first study on Wags concludes.

The likes of Becky Vardy and Coleen Rooney might need help because of all they deal with, it is claimed.



Researchers at Leeds Beckett University — who spoke to seven women — found that being a Wag could be an “invasive force that could threaten or harm their identity and self-esteem”.

The Wags, aged between 23 and 34, told of their struggles to deal with online trolls, other women, and their own partners.



One said: “I know girls who sleep with football players and then take their watches or ask for a payout, so they don’t tell their wives.”

Others told of death threats over their appearance.



Another added: “There’s an added pressure of being a partner of a player, 100 per cent.”

They all spoke of their own needs having to “take a back seat” for the men.

The researchers found the Wags played a “critical yet under-recognised role in player well-being and performance”.

However, they said that clubs rarely considered their welfare was important.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Everton in stunning transfer talks over incredible swap involving Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil
Sports.content:
CRYSTAL PALACE and Everton are in talks over swapping Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil.

Both players are thought to be keen on moving and the deal will not involve a fee.



Toffees winger McNeil, 26, nearly joined the Eagles on a loan-to-buy in February but the switch collapsed.

Johnson, 25, has had a torrid time at Selhurst Park since his £35million arrival from Tottenham in January, failing to score in 26 games.



The Wales wideman did, however, lift the Conference League.

It was his second European title in two years, having scored the winner for Spurs against Manchester United in the Europa League final 12 months earlier.



McNeil has played more than 100 games for Everton following his move from Burnley four years ago.

The Toffees have signed Hayden Hackney and Tyrique George for £24m from Middlesbrough and Chelsea respectively as well as Merlin Rohl from Freiburg for £19m.

The Toffees also saw key figures getting released, like Seamus Coleman and Idrissa Gueye.

Palace, on the other hand, landed free agents Oscar Mingueza and Takehiro Tomiyasu.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Former Arsenal defender Tomiyasu, 27, was on trial with the Eagles after playing for Japan at the 2026 World Cup and earned a contract after a recent injury hell.

Pierre Sage also replaced Oliver Glasner, who rolled credits on his glittering two-year stint at Selhurst Park that saw him winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League.

And Palace sold key defender Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea for £51m.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola offers brutal Liverpool assessment as Reds 'cannot sustain their level'
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola offers brutal Liverpool assessment as Reds 'cannot sustain their level'

Liverpool let a two-goal lead slip for the second time in pre-season as Andoni Iraola lost his first match at Anfield and then offered up a worrying assessment of where the team is at

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola has shied away from admitting Liverpool's flaws - which are alarming

Andoni Iraola admits Liverpool "cannot sustain their level" after another collapse saw them fall to defeat against Monaco.

‌



The Reds are having to get to grips to life under Iraola, who was hired as Arne Slot's replacement, and it is taking time for the team to adapt to his methods. The ex-Bournemouth boss was renowned for his high energy system whilst in charge of the Cherries.

‌



Liverpool are clearly in an adaptation phase with the first warning signs on show during their loss to Leeds over in the United States. They let a two-goal lead slip and ended up losing 4-2 to the Whites.

‌



On Sunday their inability to last the course was again exposed as they squandered a two-goal lead against Monaco, this time at Anfield. It was Iraola's first game at his new home but things soon collapsed after Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz had scored in the first-half.

Liverpool show familiar concern as three players shine in Monaco defeat - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Liverpool given Ronald Araujo transfer update as Hansi Flick makes Barcelona admission READ MORE :

The French side staged a fightback and Paris Brunner was able to cap their comeback in a five-goal thriller with Iraola not hiding anything with his assessment.

Iraola told LFC TV: "It was quite similar to the game we played against Leeds. We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don't have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

‌



"We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do."

View 2 Images Letting leads slip has been a problem in pre-season for the Reds

Liverpool finished fifth last term, a steep drop off from winning the league 12 months prior, which ultimately cost Slot his job. Iraola was tasked with making the Reds title challengers once more but pre-season has showcased issues in getting his ideas across.

‌



The Reds begin their campaign away at Newcastle before games against Nottingham Forest, Ipswich and Fulham. A return to Bournemouth faces Iraola in September.

Isak has said on the new environment: "I feel like the spirit is good in the group and we're all working hard to make things work. We're going to make sure that we're ready for the start."

Sports.title: Kyle Walker relishing Championship challenge with Burnley - 'I am not becoming anyone's meme'
Sports.content:
It may be more than 15 years since Kyle Walker last graced the Championship, but his mentality hasn't changed.

The veteran defender has not played in the second tier of English football since the 2010-11 campaign, where he briefly starred in the resolute QPR team that would go on to win the league under Neil Warnock. Back then, at the age of 20, Walker was a young prospect with his whole career ahead of him. He returns to the Championship as one of the most decorated right-back's in English football with 96 caps for his country, six Premier League titles and a Champions League triumph all to his name.

But motivation will not be an issue despite all he has accomplished as he prepares for what will be his first ever full campaign in the Championship following Burnley's relegation.

"I think if I have to get motivated to play football, I should stay in bed in the morning," Walkers says. "It's a job that I'm doing that millions want to do. So if you're not motivated to play football and don't win games, I'm definitely in the wrong job."

‌



Walker turned 36 in May but insists the physical demands of an unforgiving 46-game season in the Championship is no cause for concern. He says his physical powers have not waned, attributing his "genetic gifts" to mum and dad.

Former Premier League star punished under new rule days after completing £20m transfer READ MORE :

After amassing an abundance of accolades in the game, Walker already knows he will be a target for ambitious wingers looking to make a name for themselves. But while Walker accepts he will be a scalp, he is adamant nobody will be turning him into a meme.

"I think they try to create, what is it called, memes now? They’ll try and create memes out of me and I can assure you that I am not becoming anyone’s meme," Walker says.

"So when you come against me, I'll give it 100 percent. If you beat me on the day, you know, you shake hands at the end of the game, and you say it's a good game. I'm not rolling out anything to become a meme."

‌



Walker was earmarked for greatness long before he had a chance to truly get to grips with the relentless cut and thrust of the Championship; Tottenham snapped him up from his boyhood club, Sheffield United, in the summer of 2009 after just a handful of senior appearances.

A return to his beloved Bramall Lane followed in the form of a loan spell but it was his temporary stint at QPR which was the catalyst for the trophy-laden career Walker has gone on to enjoy.

"Playing in the Championship - it grounds you, but it also teaches you. It can be very humbling as well," he adds, referencing the wealth of experience that inhabited said QPR dressing room.

View 4 Images Burnley were relegated from the Premier League last season (Image: Alex Livesey)

‌



"We had a very good team. Neil Warnock took me and I played every game and then I went to Aston Villa for the last part of the season. I fell back in love with football a bit - I wouldn’t say I’d fallen out of love - but I went on loan from Tottenham, got called back and didn't really play as many games as I wanted. And then Harry [Redknapp] let me go back [out] on loan to get some games under my belt.

"I loved it. I probably didn’t want to leave to go to Aston Villa because I was playing football and winning every game, but it was something that I needed to do personally to make that step up to the Premier League."

From there, the Sheffield-born defender never looked back. Months later he won his first senior England cap. He then became a staple in the Tottenham team before a blockbuster transfer to Manchester City, where Walker acquired his taste for silverware.

After eight seasons in sky blue, Walker left City permanently last year with 15 major trophies to his name in order to embark on a new challenge with Burnley; a move which presented Walker with an opportunity to escape the 'noise' that becomes a non-negotiable extra for those who operate at the truly elite level.

‌



He explains: "The scrutiny is not as big, but I think then you probably scrutinise yourself more because you’re so used to achieving and winning a lot more games. You look back at yourself and think ‘What could I have done?’.

"Last season, most of all, it was about the mental game. I can play the game of football; that didn’t stop just because I went to Burnley. But mentally it was different and something that I had to channel into. But then that’s something I can pass onto the younger players now and hopefully give my experience."

View 4 Images Burnley and Wolves will both bid to make an instant return to the Premier League along with West Ham (Image: Matt McNulty)

As Walker alludes to, after almost a decade at a club where success has become almost synonymous, last year was a different experience altogether. The beleaguered Clarets suffered a death by a thousand cuts, winning just four Premier League games all season.

‌



There is an "obligation" for he and those who have stayed at the club to right the wrongs of that chastening campaign, says Walker, who adds that relegation has left a "sour taste" in the mouth.

While some have moved on, he had no qualms about returning to the level that helped truly elevate his career, even if a Championship encore was not on his footballing bucket list.

"It’s our job," he says. "Things aren’t always going to go as planned. This season might not go as planned. It might not be as plain sailing as we all want it to be. But I feel with the quality, what we have in the dressing room, that’s what we should be doing: getting promoted and going back to the Premier League."

Nicky Hayen has been tasked with achieving that feat following a protracted manager search earlier this summer. The Belgian previously impressed with Genk and Walker's first impressions of the 45-year-old have been positive.

‌



"He has been great," says Walker of Hayen. "The information he has given is key, he is very direct and I feel when a manager comes in they can give you sometimes too much information."

Burnley have immediately been installed as one of the favourites for promotion and Hayen will harbour ambitions of emulating the feats overseen by Vincent Kompany. Walker's former Manchester City team-mate masterminded a memorable promotion campaign for Burnley back in 2022-23, losing just three games and racking up an impressive 101 points.

View 4 Images Walker has picked the brains of his former Manchester City team-mate and Burnley manager, Vincent Kompany (Image: Nathan Stirk)

Walker has already picked the brains of the Bayern Munich boss, revealing: "I've spoken to Vinny, I've got words from him. How did he find it after achieving what he’s achieved? He says it’s difficult. It is something that is going to be attached to yourself personally [the expectation to win] but it is also very enjoyable.

‌



"You become a big fish again, and you get a little bit more of the ball, and it's a bit more of the game that I'm used to playing at Manchester City.

"So, hopefully, we can replicate that for when Vinny went up because I think they broke 100 points and kind of tore the Championship apart."

Now in the twilight years of his career, Walker argued that staying up last season would have been equivalent to a seventh Premier League title. That wasn't to be, but a Championship crown would go some way to quenching Walker's insatiable thirst for more achievements.

"There's always losing in football and there's always achieving in football," Walker says. "All the time I've got a football shirt on my back, I'll always give my all and I won't settle for anything less. I've got a bar for myself, but I've also got a bar more importantly for the team, and if anyone falls underneath that, then they will be told that it's not acceptable.

‌



"But hopefully, from what I've seen in pre-season, what I've seen in training, and obviously from the manager and everything like that, we're all going in the same direction — and that's to get this club back to the Premier League."

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso steps in as new Chelsea set-piece coach in heated clash with rival
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso steps in as new Chelsea set-piece coach in heated clash with rival

Chelsea were held during pre-season as they drew with Johor Darul Ta'zim but tempers flared on the touchline which saw new Blues coach Austin MacPhee at the centre of the scuffle

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso had to step in to pull apart an incident on the touchline

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was forced to step in and pull one of his coaches away from a brawl as tempers flared during their pre-season friendly with Johor Darul Ta'zim.

‌



The Blues have just hired Austin MacPhee from Aston Villa and he reacted angrily after seeing Chelsea striker Liam Delap on the receiving end of a nasty challenge. With just over an hour on the clock, defender Antonio Glauder went through the back of Delap with a strong tackle.

‌



His Chelsea team-mates were left fuming with the challenge as centre-half Tosin Adarabioyo lead the response. The Blues’ new set piece coach MacPhee was also raging, which saw Alonso having to hold him back after a clash with one of the Johor coaching staff

‌



Delap, who had converted two penalties during the match, was able to continue and Glauder went on to score a late own goal which allowed Chelsea to secure a 3-3 draw.

Man Utd in driving seat to beat Arsenal and Aston Villa to wonderkid transfer READ MORE :

Chelsea and Real Madrid eye Martin Zubimendi as Arsenal set price after Bruno Guimaraes transfer READ MORE :

The Blues will now head home from their Far East tour with Alonso's side playing Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on Saturday ahead of their Premier League opener, which sees them head to neighbours Fulham on August 24.

MacPhee has been bought in from Aston Villa as Alonso assembles his own staff in west London. MacPhee and his long blonde locks had become a fixture alongside Unai Emery and he was crucial behind the scenes as the Midlands side enjoyed their recent success.

‌



Chelsea are embarking on another season which has them being led by a new manager. The club's owners have not yet stuck with a manager for more than 18 months but none of their hires have had the pedigree of Alonso.

View 2 Images The new Chelsea coach reacted angrily to a challenge on Liam Delap

The Spaniard arrives having led Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen. His spell in Spain was short lived but by no means a disaster and his work in Germany sees him held in high regard. With Leverkusen he won the Bundesliga, ending Bayern Munich's dominance, and also claimed the German Cup.

Article continues below

Chelsea are looking to bounce back from a dire campaign that saw them finish in mid-table and go through three managers as Enzo Maresca, Liam Rosenior and Calum McFarlane all had spells leading the team.

Sports.title: Inside Italy's talks with Pep Guardiola and real reason he snubbed job amid England links
Sports.content:
Inside Italy's talks with Pep Guardiola and real reason he snubbed job amid England links

Italy pursued Pep Guardiola this summer and can close to landing him as their next manager - but the former Man City boss ultimately wanted time away after also saying no to England

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola was offered a return to management just weeks after leaving Man City (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Paolo Maldini has claimed that Pep Guardiola was so close to becoming the next Italy boss that he started jotting down possible line-ups on a piece of paper.

‌



Maldini was hired by the Azzurri in the aftermath of their World Cup qualification failure as they looked to rebuild. His remit was to hire a new manager and, after eyeing up Carlo Ancelotti, they turned their attention to Guardiola after his Manchester City exit.

‌



Talks were held with the Catalan, who has ambitions to manage in the international game. Maldini admits that Guardiola's decision to turn down the job was purely based on his desire to take some time out after a decade at the Etihad.

‌



The 55-year-old wasn't motivated by money and Maldini claimed in an interview with Corriere della Sera: "Guardiola told us: 'Give me one euro less than what the last coach was earning and I am ready'."

Roberto Mancini named new Italy manager as Claudio Ranieri makes shock return READ MORE :

Italy in turmoil as legend ready to quit 16 days into job after manager pick blocked READ MORE :

After holding talks with Guardiola in Barcelona Maldini revealed: "With Guardiola we studied the lists of players, starting from the under-17 team and above" and said that he "even began writing out line-ups".

After the ex-City boss and Ancelotti had turned down the role Maldini turned to Andrea Pirlo, one of the players who helped Italy claim the World Cup in 2006. Since retiring he's led the likes of Juventus and was poised to take the role before several of the country's chiefs intervened due to his association with Russian betting firms.

‌



Maldini stepped down from his role with Italy after less than three weeks once Pirlo was denied the chance to lead the national side. Italy have since appointed Roberto Mancini for a second time.

View 2 Images Paolo Maldini thought he had his man when he pursued Pep Guardiola

Guardiola is poised for a period out of management, which is timely given he's been in charge of a club for 13 years in succession. Before City he had three years at Bayern Munich.

‌



Guardiola reportedly had a verbal agreement in place with England before they turned to Thomas Tuchel. He was seen as a successor to Gareth Southgate once he stepped down two years ago, and his hire would've been a major coup for the FA.

When it came to it though Guardiola chose to renew his contract with City midway through the 2024/25 season, spending another 18 months at the Etihad.

Tuchel's position has come under scrutiny following England's collapse against Argentina in the World Cup semi final. But any change is unlikely after the Football Association granted Tuchel a new contract before the tournament began.

Sports.title: Arsenal next transfer priority is clear after Vinicius Jr blow and Borussia Dortmund defeat
Sports.content:
Arsenal next transfer priority is clear after Vinicius Jr blow and Borussia Dortmund defeat

ARSENAL 2-3 BORUSSIA DORTMUND: Mikel Arteta's Gunners conceded three goals for the second consecutive match on Sunday as they returned home to face BVB in the Emirates Cup

View 3 Images Arsenal looked vulnerable at the back as they were beaten 3-2 by Borussia Dortmund

Don't read too much into pre-season friendlies, unless of course, you are a defensive mess. Less than two weeks out from their Premier League opener against newly-promoted Coventry City, champions Arsenal are still getting warm.

‌



But having now shipped three goals in two consecutive defeats to Real Betis and Borussia Dortmund, it's becoming difficult to decipher whether this is merely ring rust or a glimpse into what life may really look like without William Saliba.

‌



Context is crucial because just over one year ago, the Gunners were stunned 3-2 at home by Villarreal in a similarly sketchy contest.

‌



A clean sheet in a ruthless 3-0 demolition of Athletic Club and one of the most-historic campaigns in the club's illustrious history then followed.

But it can also be true that Arsenal currently look fortunate that none of their direct rivals, outside of Tottenham, have drastically strengthened to date.

Man Utd in driving seat to beat Arsenal and Aston Villa to wonderkid transfer READ MORE :

Arsenal respond to Gabriel Martinelli transfer approach as Mikel Arteta lays out demands READ MORE :

While they remain firm favourites to retain their crown, their backline just isn't clicking in the absence of imperious Frenchman Saliba and there's an alarming lack of defensive depth.

‌



Ben White, who managed just 12 top-flight appearances last term is back following his MCL injury but Arsenal are currently placing great faith in his fitness record with Jurrien Timber still sidelined.

The Gunners were sliced apart for BVB's opener inside seven minutes and then exposed again as Konstantinos Karetsas, a prodigy Arsenal tracked last summer, bent home admirably.

Then just moments after Ethan Nwaneri handed Arsenal a lifeline, Arsenal were undone via a messy and chaotic set-piece.

‌



Forget marquee big-name Vinicius Junior alternatives, a versatile defender should now be among Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta's top transfer priorities

It's not time to hit the panic button yet as it's been a slightly odd pre-season all-round this summer, not just for Arsenal.

Another injury and the narrative quickly changes, however. The first expanded 48-team World Cup was gruelling for all parties, on all levels.

‌



View 3 Images Konstantinos Karetsas scored a stunning goal for Borussia Dortmund against Arsenal (Image: Justin Setterfield)

The whopping 104-game tournament was brutal on body clocks, a mental slog and that's without even considering the actual physical toll of the participating players' workload on the back of a long domestic campaign.

Arsenal, arguably more so than any other Premier League club, need to manage their stars carefully from here on in.

‌



The champions went deep in all four competitions last term while Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Gabriel Magalhaes and Saliba were all managing varying degrees of pain.

The latter ultimately paid the ultimate price for his bravery but Arteta cannot afford to witness Rice or Gabriel, in particular, break down this season as they are just too important to their Premier League title defence.

View 3 Images Gabriel Magalhaes started for Arsenal but they were still poor defensively

‌



Perhaps it's naive to perceive there will not be consequences somewhere along the line, which underlines the importance of strong recruitment work from Berta.

Bruno Guimaraes' £75million arrival - the Brazilian midfielder was presented to the Emirates Stadium crowd pre-kick-off - will help protect Rice's conditioning.

Sufficient defensive cover is also required and with just over three weeks left of the transfer window, there is still work to do.

‌



Guimaraes, now likely to debut against Como after watching on from the stands, is unquestionably a top acquisition but Arteta's left flank - one key area where there was scope for improvement - is not conclusively better than it was last season despite Christos Tzolis' eye-catching start to life in north London.

Next weekend's Community Shield collision with Manchester City in Cardiff should represent a strong yardstick as to where Arsenal are really at. Losing that fixture would not be ideal preparation for Coventry.
