3 Martinelli is into the final year of his Arsenal deal, but the club have the option to extend Credit: AFP

The 24-year-old has joined from Club Brugge on a five-year deal.

Bruno Guimaraes' arrival from Newcastle for £75million was confirmed on Saturday.

Meanwhile, Piero Hincapie has seen his loan from Bayer Leverkusen made permanent ahead of the new season.

Sports.title: Liverpool wonderkid impressed Virgil van Dijk in pre-season and could have solved centre-back crisis – but will be forced on loan
Sports.content:
Liverpool wonderkid impressed Virgil van Dijk in pre-season and could have solved centre-back crisis – but will be forced on loan

Liverpool fans have unearthed a new star in pre-season ahead of the upcoming campaign.

The Reds continued their preparations for the upcoming campaign with a 3-2 defeat against Monaco at Anfield on Sunday.

3 Ifeanyi Ndukwe produced an impressive performance for Liverpool against Monaco Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Despite suffering a 3-2 defeat to the Ligue 1 outfit, there were plenty of positives to take for Andoni Iraola's side.

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz were both on the scoresheet during the first half as Liverpool took a 2-0 lead.

However, it was centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe who caught the eye with his display during the opening 45 minutes.

The 18-year-old won three tackles as well as all four of his duels, lining up alongside Virgil van Dijk in central defence.

Ndukwe's tackles and duels won were the most of any player during the first half.

The Austria Under-21 international also completed 23 out of 24 attempted passes.

Meanwhile, one piece of skill in particular earned applause from Van Dijk after his turn left Monaco striker Mika Biereth on the floor.

talkSPORT verdict

talkSPORT's Micky Gray was equally impressed with the teenager's performance, explaining live on talkSPORT: "Played really well in that first 45 minutes, but I think it's because he hasn't played enough international football that they're struggling to get a work permit for him.

"So I think he's going to have to go out on loan.

"We know the problems that Liverpool have got in those centre-half positions.

3 Ndukwe is set to be forced to go on loan despite starring in pre-season for the Reds Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

"So that's really unfortunate for him, but I think it's a story that might linger on a little bit."

Following Ibrahima Konate's departure for Real Madrid, Liverpool have just four senior centre-backs at the club.

Of those, Van Dijk is the only one currently fit with youngsters Giovanni Leoni and Jeremy Jacquet yet to return to action after long-term injuries.

Joe Gomez is also expected to be unavailable until September due to a muscle problem.

However, Liverpool are set to announce the signing of Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona, talkSPORT understands.

3 Van Dijk is currently Liverpool's only fit senior centre-back Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Who is Ifeanyi Ndukwe?

Liverpool agreed a deal to sign Ndukwe from Austria Vienna in January, with the defender joining the club this summer.

His arrival had been delayed until after he turned 18 in March.

Ndukwe was part of the squad which travelled to the USA for the Reds' pre-season tour.

During the trip, he featured in all three matches against Sunderland, Wrexham and Leeds United.

Liverpool conclude their summer schedule with a pair of friendlies against Como at Anfield on Sunday, August 16.

Meanwhile, at international level, Ndukwe has already been called up to the Under-21 squad.

He was previously part of the Austria side which reached the final of last year's U17 World Cup in Qatar.

Despite that, Ndukwe does not meet the requirements for a UK work permit and will not be able to feature competitively for the Reds this season.

Sports.title: Lucas Digne joins European giants as Aston Villa lose another key player this summer
Sports.content:
Lucas Digne joins European giants as Aston Villa lose another key player this summer

Lucas Digne has left Aston Villa to re-join Paris Saint-Germain, it has been announced.

The French left-back returns to the club he left ten years ago after PSG triggered his release clause in a £6million deal.

5 Digne left PSG to join Barcelona in 2016 but is now back in the French capital Credit: Getty

A verbal agreement was in place last month for the defender who represented France at the World Cup.

PSG in Luc

Upon re-joining PSG, with whom he was at for three years in his first spell, Digne said: "The club has changed, it’s reached another level.

"It’s really incredible to be back here! The Campus? Everything is in place to perform at the very highest level.”

Digne continued: "I can’t wait to see Marquinhos again. We signed for the club at the same time, and now he’s captain and has had an incredible journey, it’s fantastic for him!

"I know Luis Enrique from Barcelona, we had a very good experience together.

"I’m looking forward to seeing my France teammates, but also other people I got to know during my first spell here, such as the kit men. It’s really nice and you quickly feel at home.

“I’m coming back as a man. I’m also a different player. I’ve gained more maturity and experience, and I want to bring that experience to the squad and win lots of trophies.

"This club is built to win, it’s in its DNA. This squad is extremely ambitious, it proves that year after year, and that’s why everyone wants to come and play in Paris.”

Digne isn't the only key player to have left Villa Park this summer with midfielder Youri Tielemans moving to Manchester United in a £35m deal, while forward Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea in a British record deal.

Digne signed for Aston Villa from Everton in 2022, making 182 appearances for the club in all competitions.

5 Digne leaves Villa after four-and-a-half years of service Credit: getty

Last season, he starred for Unai Emery's side, playing 31 times in the Premier League as they secured a top-four finish.

He provided four assists in the top flight, also featuring 11 times in the Europa League as Villa went on to win the competition.

Following the campaign, Digne headed to North America for the World Cup and played six games for France.

The 64-cap defender featured in just one group game, but got more game time as the tournament wore on before France lost to eventual champions Spain in the semi-finals.

His performances attracted interest from French giants PSG, who are set to make him back-up to Nuno Mendes.

Who could replace Digne?

talkSPORT understands that Atletico Madrid star Matteo Ruggeri is the main candidate to replace Digne at Aston Villa.

It is believed that a deal could be struck in the region of £17m for the 24-year-old.

5 Ruggeri could be heading to Villa Park as Digne's replacement Credit: Getty

Ruggeri only made the move to the Wanda Metropolitano from Atalanta last summer, where he featured in 47 games across all competitions.

Villa are yet to agree personal terms with the defender, who is open to a move to a move to Midlands.

Release clause nightmare

Emery would have been planning for the new campaign with Tielemans and Digne in his ranks, however he's lost both for low fees.

Tielemans' shock switch to Manchester United materialised after the Red Devils pulled out of a deal to sign Atalanta's Ederson.

Michael Carrick has been on the lookout for new midfielders, with the Belgian being followed by Andrey Santos from Chelsea through the door.

Villa acted fast to bring in a replacement for Tielemans, as they hijacked Newcastle's move to bring in Johan Manzambi from Hoffenheim.

5 Emery has seen the club sell Digne, Tielemans and Morgan Rogers this summer Credit: Getty

5 Highly-rated midfielder Manzambi moved to Villa as a replacement for Tielemans Credit: Getty

Manzambi was close to signing for the Magpies, but he hesitated on making a decision, allowing Villa to enter talks.

Villa meanwhile have also sold Rogers to Chelsea in a £117m deal.

And they quickly replaced him with Alejandro Garnacho after snapping up the winger from the Blues on an initial loan deal.

Villa be coming up against Digne and PSG in their first competitive match of the season in the UEFA Super Cup on August 12, live on talkSPORT.

By winning the Europa League last term, they take on the Champions League winner in a battle of the European champions.

Sports.title: Rangers star stretchered off hours after club record transfer bid rejected
Sports.content:
Youssef Chermiti was stretchered off during Rangers' match against Hibernian on Sunday.

The striker was replaced by Ryan Naderi after 36 minutes at Ibrox.

3 Chermiti was stretchered off hours after Rangers rejected a club-record bid Credit: PA



It came just hours after Galatasaray saw a bid rejected for the 22-year-old.

According to Sky Sports, the offer would have represented a club-record sale for Rangers.

Their current record of £19million was set in 2023 by Calvin Bassey's move to Ajax.

According to reports in Turkey, Galatasarsay's verbal approach was worth €25million (£21.5m).



However, Rangers rejected the offer, with their valuation of Chermiti closer to €40million (£34.3m).

Any potential move now looks in doubt after an injury setback for the Portugal Under-21 international.



Chermiti was stretchered off before half time after suffering a nasty-looking injury having fallen by the advertising hoardings on the byline at Ibrox.

He had stayed down off the pitch after chasing down a loose ball in front of goal.



His withdrawal came after the hosts had conceded a 12th minute penalty to trail against Hibs.

Josh Campbell converted from 12 yards to open the scoring and heap further pressure on Derek McInnes.

3 Chermiti suffered a nasty-looking injury after colliding with the pitchside advertising boards Credit: PA

A late own goal from Miguel Chaiwa appeared to have rescued a point for Rangers.



However, Callum Wright grabbed a 93rd minute winner as the home side suffered their first league defeat of the season.

It means McInnes is still awaiting his first win as Rangers manager since joining from Hearts this summer.

His side were held by Dundee United on the opening weekend of the season before losing to Jagiellonia Bialystok in the Europa League on Thursday.

Chermiti at Rangers

Chermiti signed for Rangers from Everton on a four-year deal last summer.



He had previously spent seven years with Sporting Lisbon in his native Portugal after joining the club's academy in 2016.

3 Galatasaray's £21.5million bid for Chermiti has been rejected Credit: PA

The forward has also been capped by his country up to Under-21 level.

Since joining Rangers, Chermiti has scored 15 goals in 42 appearances for the club.

McInnes reaction

Speaking to Premier Sports following his side's latest defeat, McInnes admitted: "We were guilty of passing up opportunities in the first half and not playing forward enough.



"I've seen it back, I don't think it's a penalty but we have a lot of the game to try and rectify that. I thought it was very soft and surprised the referee is brought over (to the monitor) for it.

"When the ball did go into our strikers we were far more effective and I felt the equaliser was deserved and we wanted to win the game. I can't fault my players' effort.

"There are little things going against us at the minute but we have to stay strong, we're not as bad as people think.

"At the minute we are trying to work boys back to the same level of fitness and trying to manage that situation.



"I understand the fan frustration, they want and expect to see their team win. I share the frustration."

Sports.title: Arsenal wonderkid tipped to be better than Ethan Nwaneri and fulfil his potential
Sports.content:
Arsenal wonderkid tipped to be better than Ethan Nwaneri and fulfil his potential

Max Dowman is destined to live up to his potential - he's only going to get better and will be given more chances to shine.

That's the view of Arsenal cult hero Perry Groves, who rubbished any speculation that the 16-year-old could grow impatient over game time in the coming months.



4 Arsenal starlet Dowman is considered to be one of the world's top prospects Credit: Getty

Dowman enjoyed a record-breaking breakthrough 2025/26 season in which he become the youngest player to win the Premier League.

The versatile teenager, who can operate as both a right winger or attacking midfielder, also holds the record as the youngest goalscorer in competition.

That is in addition to being the youngest player to start a Premier League game, while also being the youngest to feature in the Champions League - doing so aged 15 and 308 days old.



In total, Dowman featured 13 times last campaign as Arsenal ended 22 years of top-flight woe, with the player since featuring heavily in pre-season.

With Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke yet to be involved in pre-season action having been given an extended break following England's run to the World Cup semi-finals, Dowman could start in next week's Community Shield clash against Manchester City.



To the Max

Arsenal and England fans are hopeful he can be the future of the two teams in the years to come.

But speaking on the Sunday Session, legendary broadcaster Ian 'The Moose' Abrahams questioned whether Dowman will become frustrated in the upcoming season.



He argued that he may struggle to deal with Saka and Madueke ahead of him in the pecking order as he continues to force his way into Mikel Arteta's thinking.

Abrahams likened his situation to that of fellow Hale End graduate Ethan Nwaneri's, insisting the 19-year-old opted to join Marseille on loan January because of a lack of first-team chances.

Nwaneri was considered Arsenal's jewel of their academy when he became the Premier League youngest's player when he came on against Brentford in September 2022 at the age of 15 years and 181 days old.

4 Nwaneri was on target in Arsenal's Emirates Cup defeat to Borussia Dortmund on Sunday Credit: Getty



He then scored nine goals from 37 games during his breakthrough 2024/25 campaign, before falling down the pecking order last term.

But Groves insisted that Dowman is only going to be given more minutes by Arteta as he showcases his talent every time he graces the pitch.

He said: "It won't be a problem, Max Dowman when you compare [them], he's a different level to Nwaneri.

"I haven't seen a player of that age with that amount of natural ability.



"And the other thing with Max Dowman, normally players with that low centre of gravity and brilliant ball carriers, they're normally about 5ft 8in, 5ft 9in - he's 6ft tall - and he's got a bit of an edge.

"The game against Girona [4-1 pre-season win], where he scored a goal and made one, the goal that he scored, Alex Moreno, who used to play for Aston Villa, he was trying to rough him up.

4 Dowman and Nwaneri could battle for minutes against each other in the upcoming season for the Gunners Credit: Getty

"And Max Dowman palmed him off, he put a palm in his chest and Moreno fell on the floor and pretended like he had been hit on the head.



"So I must admit, I don't think that you're gonna have a problem with Max Dowman.

"He will get more minutes, he's always going to be on the bench, he'll play in the Carabao Cup games, so I can't see a problem with him this season at all."

Dowman distractions?

Abrahams once again raised concern that some of the country's greatest prospects have ultimately failed to live up to their early hype, as he pointed out off-field distractions could soon come into play.

He remarked: "I probably will be proved wrong in having any concerns about him, but I've done this job for 35 years.



"I've seen so many really good, unbelievable prospects, 'This guy is the best that this clubs ever produced' or 'This country has ever produced.'

4 Dowman wrote himself into the Premier League history books in March - becoming the youngest ever goalscorer Credit: Getty

"And for one reason or another, some of them may be footballing reasons, some of them may not be footballing reasons, it may not quite have happened for them.

"I hope this happens for him, I hope he becomes a Ballon d'Or winner in four or five years time, I hope he goes on to dominate for club and country.



"I think he has got pretty much everything, but he is only 16-and-a-half, he's still got to do several things which he hasn't even thought about yet.

"Growing, girls, cars, money... all those sorts of things don't matter to him at the moment, because all that matters to him is football and maybe his education up until now.

"But all those life things will come into play later on, and how will he deal with those?

"And I'm hoping that he'll be able to deal with it, so we can all say that this is the best player that England has ever produced."

Sports.title: Donald Trump whips up LIV Golf fans as he rides around with Gary Player on final day of tournament at his New Jersey course
Sports.content:
President Donald Trump spent the day at his Bedminster golf course once again as LIV Golf played its final round.

Trump was on hand for the LIV Golf New York event toward the end of the rebel tour's season.

The day before, the President was spotted on a golf cart driving around as he was followed by security and his daughter, Ivanka.

On Sunday, he was joined by legendary golfer Gary Player on the cart as they watched the action.

The President also got out of his cart and strolled onto one of the tee boxes, waving to fans and supporters.

It's the second day that Trump has been at the event for the struggling golf circuit.

President Donald Trump was joined by Gary Player during LIV Golf New York's final round

The last round of the tournament was held at Trump's golf course in Bedminster, New Jersey

At one point, the Commander-in-Chief even strolled onto the tee box during the tournament

Trump arrived in the area on Friday evening as Air Force One touched down just before 6:00pm ET.

The Presidential motorcade then shepherded him to the course through a nasty thunderstorm that swept across the Northeastern United States.

Trump has been a longtime supporter of the rebel tour that was formerly backed by the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF).

Earlier this year, the PIF announced they would stop financially supporting LIV Golf after the conclusion of the current season.

Earlier this week, LIV announced they had secured funding for the 2027 season, but little further details were revealed.

Over the course of its existence, LIV Golf has frequented golf courses owned by the President's holding company.

Earlier this year, the tournament was held at Trump National Golf Club in Washington, DC.

LIV has also hosted a Miami event at the Blue Monster course at Trump National Doral in the past.

LIV has played at multiple Trump-owned golf courses throughout its existence

The President has previously tried to end the civil war between LIV Golf and the PGA Tour

In the past, Trump has attempted to bring a peaceful conclusion to the civil war between LIV and the PGA Tour.

'I do believe that all of the golfers should be playing against each other. They were viewing something as a monopoly, but it's swaying away. It should be the opposite of a monopoly,' Trump told reporters in April.

'I want to see Rory [McIlroy] playing Bryson DeChambeau. I want to see big Jon Rahm playing Scottie, who is so great. Scottie Scheffler is great.

'They have great players on LIV, but it's almost like people want to see that. That's why the Masters was so good, because you saw everybody together.'

Sports.title: The ORIGINAL spygate: John Terry claims Jose Mourinho showed Chelsea stars rival's training footage on eve of game in new Netflix documentary
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho was spying on opposition teams' training sessions while Southampton manager Tonda Eckert was still playing football for his secondary school team

The now-infamous Spygate, which was broken exclusively by Daily Mail Sport and involved Eckert and his Saints side, stole the headlines for weeks upon weeks back in May.

It saw the Saints expelled from the Championship play-off final, after admitting to spying on Middlesbrough and two other rivals.

But it turns out that former Chelsea boss Mourinho was participating in the incendiary practice long before it became trendy.

That's according to former Chelsea captain John Terry, who has revealed in the new three-part Netflix docu-series titled MOURINHO – which is due to be released on Tuesday – that Mourinho once managed to get hold of footage of a rival's training session during his first season in charge of the Blues.

In the documentary, Terry said: 'I remember, we were due to play Bolton and up on the screen is Bolton's training session from the day before.

The new three-part Netflix docu-series titled MOURINHO has revealed that the former Chelsea boss once got hold of a rival's training session before playing them

John Terry revealed in the documentary that Mourinho got a hold of a Bolton Wanderers training session in his first season at the club.

'And Big Sam [Allardyce] was like "hit Gallas, he's not very good in the air" and he was like spitting on the mic.

'It was just like, wow. Who gets footage from someone's training ground? I'm actually still not sure where he got the footage from.'

It is unclear whether this was ahead of the home or away fixture during that season, in which Chelsea secured their first Premier League title.

If it was ahead of the clash at Stamford Bridge in November 2004, then, much like in the case of Eckert and Southampton, Mourinho's shady tactics failed to have the desired outcome as Chelsea drew 2-2 with Sam Allardyce's side.

However, if the spying was done ahead of the reverse fixture, then it proved fruitful as Chelsea famously secured the title at the then-named Reebok Stadium, with Frank Lampard scoring a brace in a 2-0 win.

The practice of spying has certainly become much more popular in the two decades that have since passed, with Marcelo Bielsa also found to have instructed a colleague to snoop on Derby County's training ahead of a Championship game in 2019.

Leeds were fined £200,000 and reprimanded by the EFL after the club admitted a breach of Regulation 3.4, which states: 'In all matters and transactions relating to the League, each club shall behave towards each other club and The League with the utmost good faith.'

Sports.title: 'There were tears': Frank Lampard and John Terry open up on Jose Mourinho's emotional exit from Chelsea in 2007 as Portuguese coach reveals how his relationship with Roman Abramovich fell apart
Sports.content:
'There were tears': Frank Lampard and John Terry open up on Jose Mourinho's emotional exit from Chelsea in 2007 as Portuguese coach reveals how his relationship with Roman Abramovich fell apart

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Frank Lampard and John Terry have lifted the lid on the Chelsea squad's emotional reaction to Jose Mourinho's first departure from the club.

Mourinho enjoyed two spells as Blues boss, winning three Premier League titles during his time at the helm.

Two of those titles came during his first tenure at Stamford Bridge, as the self-proclaimed 'Special One' began life in England with back-to-back titles. However, cracks began to appear during his second season in charge.

The new three-part Netflix docu-series titled MOURINHO, which is due to be released on Tuesday, has delved into how Mourinho's first stint at Chelsea unravelled before his eventual sacking in September 2007.

Lampard and Terry were Chelsea's two most important players during Mourinho's glory days, and during the documentary outlined just how much his exit affected them personally, and the squad.

‘I remember him coming into the dressing room and he said to me that he’d been sacked,' Lampard explained.

Frank Lampard (left, pictured in 2005) and John Terry (right) were deeply affected by Jose Mourinho's first departure from Chelsea in 2007

'I couldn’t think about how much this man had helped my career, how much I loved working with him. There were tears, which is not normal in the dressing room when a manager leaves.’

Former Chelsea skipper Terry made much of his adoration for Mourinho known in the documentary, stating that ‘I would leave that pitch in a coffin for him.' And almost two decades on, he puts blame on himself for the manager's exit.

‘You’ve got grown men, tears running down their face, not really understanding why. And even still today I’m like, that’s my fault.

'When we drew the Champions League game [with Rosenborg], my man scored. If I didn’t let that person score, would he have lasted another couple of years? Who knows? I still feel kind of responsible for that, if that makes sense.

'It’s just disappointing how it all ended, if I’m honest. I absolutely loved him and adored him and was more upset than anyone, to be honest.’

Mourinho made it clear that his relationship with then-owner Roman Abramovich had become increasingly fractious as the seasons went by, despite the success the Blues were having on the pitch.

‘In my work, the triangle: Jose, Peter Kenyon (former chief executive), Roman was invaded by strangers.

'In the beginning, you play at Stamford Bridge, you look to the box, Roman, his wife, with one or two persons of his confidence. A few seasons later: former players, agents. These kinds of people, they know where the money is.’

Terry became emotional when talking about Mourinho's exit in the new docu-series about the former Chelsea manager

The documentary also outlined the breakdown in Mourinho's relationship with then-owner Roman Abramovich (pictured in 2004)

The former Chelsea boss also recalled a bizarre incident that affected his relationship with Abramovich, which saw the Russian request him to leave club training to help manage a group of strangers abroad as a favour.

‘I think Roman changed,' Mourinho continued. 'For example, one day Peter came to me quite embarrassed and he told me,"Jose, I have to tell you something.

'"The boss is in Sardinia with these boats, and the people that work in these boats they play football against guys from the hotel, and they are losing. Can you go there to win a game for him?”“No, Peter, I have training today. I have to prepare for tomorrow; I cannot go”.

'And he [Roman] was not happy with that.’

The pair did go on to mend their relationship in the end, with Mourinho turning down the opportunity to become Sir Alex Ferguson's successor at Manchester United in 2013 in order to return to Stamford Bridge.

In the docu-series Mourinho extraordinarily revealed that he verbally agreed to take over at Old Trafford before making a dramatic U-turn in order to re-join the Blues.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho REFUSES to apologise to former Chelsea team doctor Eva Carneiro over infamous 'daughter of a wh***' touchline row as he finally addresses row 11 years later: 'I always use my vocabulary when I'm not happy'
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho REFUSES to apologise to former Chelsea team doctor Eva Carneiro over infamous 'daughter of a wh***' touchline row as he finally addresses row 11 years later: 'I always use my vocabulary when I'm not happy'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jose Mourinho has avoided apologising to Dr Eva Carneiro after opening up about their infamous touchline row for the first time in over a decade.

The former Chelsea boss has spoken about the incident in his new three-part Netflix docu-series titled MOURINHO, which marks the first time he has done so since agreeing a settlement with the club's former doctor in 2016.

During a Premier League clash with Swansea City at the start of the 2015-16 season, Mourinho hit the roof when Carneiro and physio Jon Fearn went onto the pitch to treat Eden Hazard, who had gone down seemingly injured.

Dr Carneiro claimed that Mourinho sexually discriminated against her during his tirade and called her the 'daughter of a wh***' in his native Portuguese.

Back in 2015, Mourinho called her 'impulsive and naive' in his first public reaction to her decision to treat Hazard. She was then dropped from first-team duties and left the club just a month later.

Mourinho and Chelsea eventually agreed a settlement after Carneiro took them to a tribunal over claims that she was discriminated against by the manager, and constructively dismissed by the club.

Jose Mourinho had an infamous touchline spat with Dr Eva Carneiro during a Chelsea match in 2015

The 63-year-old has spoken up about the incident for the first time in over a decade in Netflix's new three-part docu-series MOURINHO

But 11 years on, Mourinho believes he treated Carneiro in the same manner that he would treat a male doctor.

‘For me, a lady doctor is the same as a man’s doctor,' Mourinho said in the docu-series. 'So, as always, I use my vocabulary when I’m not happy.

'There are words in moments where the tension is very, very high. Normally, people with football culture, with football DNA, with football background, they go over it in one second. In that case, it was different.’

Hazard, who played under the now-63-year-old for two years, claimed 'it was nothing special' in the documentary, which is set to air on Tuesday, but 'with Jose everything is bigger'.

Footage shows that the Portuguese coach, who is now Real Madrid manager, shouted a whole host of expletives toward Carneiro and Fearn as they treated Hazard. He screamed phrases such as 'f*** off, man' and 'f*** you, man'.

'I’m not a doctor, but my eyes know when a player is injured, and they know when a player is not injured,' Mourinho said in the docu-series.

'I knew that he was not injured, but the doctors went to the pitch, and in that moment we were left with nine players.’

Hazard was forced to come off the pitch for a brief period, as is the rule when a player receives medical treatment, leaving Chelsea with nine men after Thibaut Courtois had been sent off.

John Terry, who was Chelsea's captain during both of Mourinho's stints at Stamford Bridge, claimed it was well known by both players and staff that the manager did not want his

Speaking in MOURINHO, he said: ‘Medically, he would say unless it’s really, really bad, then they’re [the team doctors] not coming on. That was the understanding for us as players; the medical staff, everyone bought into that.

‘It was a big moment obviously and he took a lot of backlash for that. There was a lot of heat on the football club.’

Carneiro left Chelsea one month after the incident after being dropped from first-team duties

Mourinho agreed a settlement with the club's former doctor after going to tribunal

Chelsea gave Dr Carneiro an unreserved apology, but Mourinho refused to say sorry and grinned as he left the tribunal.

A deal was done in a back corridor of the court and Chelsea then issued a statement saying it 'regretted the circumstances' which led to former club doctor leaving and 'apologises unreservedly to her and her family for the distress caused'.

The terms of the settlement remain secret, but during the tribunal it was revealed that Chelsea had previously offered £1.2million to silence Carneiro.

Mourinho did not apologise after the incident or at the tribunal and there were no signs of an apology in the docu-series either.

The three-part documentary combs through the career of Mourinho, covering the various highs and lows from his three decades in the professional game, from his winning mentality and undeniable ability to secure silverware to his many, many controversies.

Terry and Frank Lampard are just two of a host of Mourinho's former players who provide anecdotes and insight into the manager, who has won 26 major trophies during his career on the touchline.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho makes stunning admission that he AGREED to replace Sir Alex Ferguson as Man United manager in 2013 before making U-turn during emotional phone call with legendary boss
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho has extraordinarily revealed that he 'signed' to become Sir Alex Ferguson's replacement at Manchester United in 2013, before going back on his decision to re-join Chelsea.

Mourinho, 63, managed the Red Devils between 2016 and 2018, but has now admitted for the first time that he agreed to take charge of the club three years prior.

The Portuguese coach had just left Real Madrid in dramatic circumstances and was on the lookout for his next project when he was approached by United and Sir Alex.

Ferguson was looking for his successor after he left the club following a trophy-laden 26 years at the helm, and until now, it was believed that the managerial legend only had eyes for David Moyes.

However, speaking in his new three-part Netflix docu-series, Mourinho dropped the bombshell that he was actually Ferguson's first-choice.

'I go to Chelsea in 2013. But in that period, there is something that nobody knows,' said the now Real Madrid boss in MOURINHO, which is set to air on Tuesday.

Jose Mourinho has revealed he agreed to become Sir Alex Ferguson's replacement at Man United in 2013

The Portuguese coach dropped the bombshell in his new Netflix docu-series titled MOURINHO

'I think I can say because I don't hurt anyone with the truth. And I think the objective of the work that we are doing is to tell the truth. When I left Real Madrid, I signed with Manchester United to go to Manchester United after Sir Alex.'

Following the stunning statement, the documentary then shows Ferguson confirming that he had indeed asked Mourinho to take over from him at United.

Ferguson said: ‘He was offered the job, yes. I sat him down and explained the situation, and as far as I was concerned, he was accepting. And then within hours, it changed.'

Despite seemingly verbally agreeing with Ferguson to become his successor, Mourinho made a dramatic U-turn and instead decided to go back to his former club Chelsea, six years after his initial departure.

'Early evening, he phoned me, and he was crying,' Ferguson continued. He said, “I can’t take it, I’ve given my word to Chelsea, and I’m not going to break my word”.

'The reason he gave to me, I can understand, but I was disappointed.’

Mourinho was coming off the back of a turbulent season at Real Madrid, in which he and various members of the squad had fallen out. Sami Khedira, former Real midfielder and now Mourinho's assistant, even described the dressing room as a 'nightmare' to be a part of.

And that difficult end to his tenure in Madrid, where he has now returned to, played a key part in his decision to return to Chelsea rather than take over at United.

'I was of course very flattered because Man United has an incredible appeal,' Mourinho added. 'When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Manchester United is very, very close.

'But one thing is love for football, and another thing is love for a certain club. I think this is more powerful than love for football, and fundamentally after Real Madrid, I needed to feel that I’m loved.

Sir Alex Ferguson confirmed Mourinho agreed to be his successor before making a u-turn

Mourinho decided to re-join Chelsea instead and says that he 'did it for love'

‘For me to lose the chance to be the coach to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson was dramatic. But I don’t regret because it was a decision I made with my heart.

'I think it is [Friedrich] Nietzsche (the philosopher) who said something that when you do something for love, you are never doing anything wrong. I did it for love.’

Mourinho ended up spending two years back at the Blues, winning a third Premier League title of his career and a League Cup.

Meanwhile, Ferguson's successor Moyes lasted just nine months in the job, and the Red Devils have yet to win another Premier League since the division's most successful-ever manager left Old Trafford.

Mourinho did eventually end up at United, and managed to win the League Cup and the UEFA Europa League in his first season at the club before leading them to a second-place Premier League finish in 2017-18.

But his tenure quickly unravelled during his third season with poor results and a fallout with several prominent players – including £89million Paul Pogba – led to his sacking in December of his third season.

Sports.title: Everton and Crystal Palace in advanced talks over Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson swap deal - as Trevoh Chalobah joins Como in £25.7m move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Everton and Crystal Palace in advanced talks over Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson swap deal - as Trevoh Chalobah joins Como in £25.7m move: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Everton and Palace advance in swap deal talks

Everton and Crystal Palace are advancing in talks over a swap deal involving Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil.

Initial discussions last week were described as complicated over the difference in value; Johnson, 25, cost £35million from Tottenham when he joined in January and has four years left on contract.

McNeil, 26, was valued at £20m when he saw a move to Palace collapse in January and has one year remaining on contract.

Everton and Crystal Palace are advancing in talks over a swap deal involving Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil

However, talks between the two clubs are now progressing over a compromise.

Johnson has been a long-term target for Everton and David Moyes, dating back to his spell at Nottingham Forest. He joined Palace for a then-club record transfer fee, in the winter window but has struggled badly to find any form and there is a growing sense a move would suit all parties.

McNeil was upset when he failed to get his move away in January but regained his place under Moyes. If all goes well a deal both players could be given permission to undergo medicals early this week.

Meanwhile, Palace are keen to offer a new contract for Jefferson Lerma while Club Brugge are pushing to agree a £10m deal plus sell-on for Pakace's Romain Esse.

Digne returns to PSG

France defender Lucas Digne has completed his return to Paris St Germain from Aston Villa on a three-year contract.

The 33-year-old full-back, who featured in six of Les Bleus' World Cup matches, had two years left on his contract with the midlands club, with PSG triggering a release clause.

Digne, who started his professional career with Lille, made 30 Ligue 1 appearances in a three-year spell at PSG until 2016, when he moved on to Barcelona.

France defender Lucas Digne has completed his return to Paris St Germain from Aston Villa

He told PSG's website: 'I am very honoured to be returning to Paris St Germain following the wonderful experience I had here more than 10 years ago.

'I am particularly impressed by how the club has developed over the years. The working conditions at the Campus are exceptional and reflect the club's ambitions.

'I can't wait to start this new chapter and put all my experience at the service of the team. Once again, I will give my very best to defend the colours of Paris St Germain.'

JAMES DUTTON

Chalobah's Italian Job

Trevoh Chalobah has completed his move from Chelsea to Italian side Como in a deal worth more than £30million.

England defender Chalobah departs Stamford Bridge for an initial £25.7m plus a further £5.1m in potential add-ons, as revealed by Window Watch last week.

The 27-year-old has signed a contract until 2031 with the Serie A club, who are managed by former Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas and are preparing for their first season in the Champions League.

Trevoh Chalobah has completed his move from Chelsea to Italian side Como in a deal worth more than £30million

Chalobah made 151 appearances for the Blues, including 47 last term, after joining the club's academy at under-nine level.

He said: 'I'm thrilled and honoured to be here at Como. It's an ambitious, rising project and working with manager Cesc Fabregas again is truly special.

'I can't wait to bring my experience to the team, feel the incredible atmosphere at the stadium, and connect with the fans. I will give my absolute all every single day to make history together'.

JAMES DUTTON

Sunderland target Ipswich keeper

Sunderland are showing interest in Ipswich Town goalkeeper Alex Palmer.

The 29-year-old has emerged as an option for Regis Le Bris' side as Wrexham continue to push for Sunderland keeper Anthony Patterson who is valued at £8m.

Palmer is also on Wrexham's radar should a deal for Patterson fall down.

Ipswich face Sunderland in the first game of the season.

As well as Palmer, Ipswich have Christian Walton returning from injury and have signed two new Dutch keepers in Kjell Scherpen and Kayne van Oevelen.

The latter may yet go out on loan and Ipswich are among the clubs that have held interest in Newcastle United keeper Nick Pope.

Man City striker in talks with Southampton

Manchester City striker Divin Mubama has agreed to join Southampton on loan for the season.

The former West Ham forward did well on loan at Stoke City last season up until he suffered an ankle ligament injury in January, incurred by a hefty challenge against QPR.

Manchester City striker Divin Mubama has agreed to join Southampton on loan for the season

He has bounced back to full fitness though and has impressed on City's pre-season tour scoring two goals, including a composed finish against Inter Milan, and weighing in with an assist.

The 21-year-old has had interest from a number of Championship clubs including Preston North End, Middlesbrough and Derby County.

Swedish international heads to Hull

Hull City have signed Sweden international Elliot Stroud from Swedish side Mjallby for around £3.5million.

The wing-back has joined on a four-year contract, which includes an option for a an extra year.

The 24-year-old played in all four of Sweden's matches at the World Cup.

West Ham make opening Parrott bid

West Ham have made an opening offer understood to be worth around £15million for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott

West Ham have made an opening offer understood to be worth around £15million for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott and are exploring a deal for Arsenal's Reiss Nelson.

Parrott, their leading goalscorer last season, started on the bench for Alkmaar's opening league game against Den Haag on Saturday.

The Hammers are prepared to break the Championship record of over £17.5million to get Parrott amid competition from Porto.

Nelson has been on the Hammers' radar before and has attracted interest from Fulham and Benfica in this window.

The 26-year-old had an indifferent campaign on loan at Brentford last season.

The Hammers had been pursuing a loan for Sunderland's Simon Adingra but he picked up an injury and has been wearing a protective boot on his left foot.

United keen on Page

Manchester United are interested in signing Leicester prospect Louis Page.

The 18-year-old midfielder has made 21 appearances for the Foxes and won EFL Apprentice of the Year last season.

Arsenal and Aston Villa have also expressed interest in the England Under-20 international but it is understood he wants to join United.

Louis Page has impressed for Leicester and is on the radar of some top sides

Charles closes on Fulham move

Fulham have agreed a £30million deal with Southampton for midfielder Shea Charles.

The 22-year-old is expected to undergo a medical in the next 24 hours and will sign a five-year contract with the option for an extra year.

Read the full story here.

Willock on Besiktas radar

Newcastle midfielder Joe Willock remains a target for Besiktas.

The Turkish side are working on an offer for the 26-year-old but believe Newcastle's current asking price is too high.

Joe Willock is a target of Turkish side Besiktas this month

Newcastle are continuing to work on a £13m deal for Marseille's Pierre Emile Hojbjerg.

They want an experienced midfielder to work alongside new signings Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba.

Read the latest on Newcastle's summer transfer business here.

Race to sign Tuanzebe heats up

Free agent defender Axel Tuanzebe is attracting interest from Saudi Pro league and Premier League sides.

The 28-year-old centre back had an impressive World Cup on the back of a challenging season with Burnley in the top flight and is ready for a new challenge.

Axel Tuanzebe is drawing a lot of interest from both English sides and abroad

Everton and Brentford have looked at the former Manchester United academy graduate and he has drawn attention from abroad also.

He made 16 appearances and scored one goal last season and spent the two previous seasons with Ipswich Town.

Hamer closes on Cov return

Gus Hamer is due to undergo a medical after Coventry and Sheffield United agreed a £6million deal for the midfielder.

The package for the 29-year-old is worth £6m plus add-ons.

Hamer spent three years at Coventry between 2020 and 2023, becoming a real fans favourite scoring 19 goals in 132 appearances.

Blades manager Chris Wilder hinted last week that Hamer had asked to join Coventry and had already spoken to Frank Lampard. His medical is scheduled for today.

Sports.title: Journey to Wembley: Daily Mail Sport's special 50th anniversary love letter to the FA Cup begins at 'Little Wembley', the home of Nelson FC - the ninth-tier side who were first EVER British team to win at Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Journey to Wembley: Daily Mail Sport's special 50th anniversary love letter to the FA Cup begins at 'Little Wembley', the home of Nelson FC - the ninth-tier side who were first EVER British team to win at Real Madrid

The ground at Nelson FC is called ‘Little Wembley’ and however resplendent the scene at its far grander namesake where the FA Cup final is played, 286 days and 600 or so games from now, it will do well to match the inestimable beauty of Saturday, when the arc of the old competition’s journey began once more.

The oasis of green in sun-starched east Lancashire has owed a lot to the club recently inviting the local fire service to carry out a practice drill which entailed spraying a lot of water on the pitch.

Limited supplies are also being piped a few hundred yards from Pendle Water, the river you cross to reach the ground, which once powered the local cotton mill, whose 200ft chimney and stone-built workers cottages form the backdrop to one of the tournament’s 208 Preliminary Qualifying Round ties.

By 11am groundsman Trevor Stamworth is marking out the pitch, which locals took to calling 'Little Wembley' decades back because of its quality. Staff are setting up in the little bar area, where sepia images provide reminders of Nelson’s small but very significant part in football history – a 4-2 win over Real Madrid in 1923, during a tour of Spain, which made them the first British side to beat the club on their own turf.

A couple of deckchairs are set out in the front gardens of the workers’ cottages which form a warm-up area beside the pitch and Nelson manager Arron Ripley arrives at 1pm to lay out the team’s jerseys in the dressing room and hone a pre-match pep-talk which will include him reminding his players that only one in 3,400 people in Britain get to play in the FA Cup, so they should seize this day.

‘You’re just looking for the small details that might get through,’ 32-year-old Ripley reflects as we sit in the dug-out, watching his players warm-up. ‘We look to put detail on things in many ways. ‘A friend of mine who’s an analyst, puts together clips for the players and we’ve got GPS vests for every game. Our video recorder’s broken at the moment, but we usually watch games back.’

Daily Mail Sport headed to Nelson for the opening round of FA Cup ties

Nelson's 'Little Wembley' ground perfectly captures the magic of the FA Cup

Groundsman Trevor Stamworth marks out the pitch ahead of the match against Stockport Georgians

This bucolic scene on a peerless summer’s day creates the impression that there has not been a cloud in Nelson’s sky, though the reality is very different. The club has been the subject of various failed ownership experiments in recent times, leading to the club being in a state of financial peril, two years ago. The lumpy pitch always flooded, the team lost almost every week and they got barely 50 through the gate.

This coincided with local businessmen Chris Price, who is in the industrial cleaning business, learning that it might be for sale. He and a friend Stewart Fort, an engineering entrepreneur, bought it for the best part of £30,000, and have together set out on a mission to build a thriving community club and take it from tier 10 to the tier eight Northern Premier League whilst doing so.

The fruits of their labour and invention are all around the place, from the new club shop and stand, both built out of converted shipping containers, the smart, timber-built food facility and the small ‘Sponsors Lounge’, where Fort is helping lay out the knives and forks at midday. Price and Fort estimate they’ve put in £700,000, so far, with the £162,000 the FA has contributed a testament to the role the governing body is not always given full credit for.

From a near certain plunge to the West Lancashire League – a relegation spared by another club folding – Nelson won promotion to the North West Counties Premier Division last season and have started the new campaign with a win. The talk is of promotion again. But roads to recovery are neither easy nor linear in football.

Despite the co-owners laying out £32,000 on pitch drainage and £52,000 on new dressing rooms, seven of the ground’s eight floodlights have suddenly failed and contractors are currently battling to get new cables laid and get those lights back on.

Nelson aim to have 260 paying fans through the turnstiles each week

Co-owners Chris Price and Stewart Fort - who bought the club for just shy of £30,000, have turned Nelson into a local success story

Nelson's ground is called Little Wembley due to the high-quality playing surface

Fans enjoyed beers pitchside on a glorious day in east Lancashire

Here, in a microcosm, is evidence of why the FA Cup, which seems to have become a minor consideration for football’s great and good, matters so very much. Price and Fort are not petro-dollar billionaires or captains of finance and while they find the money for capital projects, the football side of things must fund itself. The more advertising boards they sell, the more resource will be available to Ripley to find players who, at this level, are paid an average of £100 a week.

‘Reaching the First Round Proper would earn us nearly £25,000 and that would make a massive difference to us,’ says Fort, as he reflects on some of the unglamorous work of the past few years here, including shifting 27 tons of muck out of the goalmouths to create the flat surface he looks out across. ‘The bigger picture is finding the 260 or so people we aim to get through the turnstiles every week. But this competition is everything for us.’

Ripley feels the significance of the income just as acutely, given that Nelson’s new ambition puts him under the same pressure that every manager knows - and contributed to the club parting company with him, just before Christmas 2024. ‘They sacked me after we’d lost five games but after my replacement didn’t get us promoted, they brought me back and last season we managed it,’ he says, ‘So yes, there’s all the pressure that comes at any ambitious club.’

That promotion has delivered Nelson to this, their first FA Cup appearance since 2017, since tier nine clubs are the lowest level who enter. ‘Over £1,000 winnings if we win today and that all goes into pot,’ Ripley says.

His managerial ethos entails being ‘very locally-driven’, with only one of his squad living more than half an hour from Nelson, and putting the time in to knowing who you’re up against. Ripley is very much part-time, too – a digital project manager with filling station operator EG – but he watched opponents Stockport Georgians beat Wythenshawe Town in the Midland League Premier a few days earlier.

The preparation shows. Nelson are stronger and quicker to the ball and, vitally, have Sefton Gonzales, a powerful and combative centre forward who works as a storeman, in their ranks. They lead through Lewis Brown, one of a Nelson midfield tandem who dominate the early stages, though no manner of opposition scouting can quell Stockport’s Lucas Berry, a former Salford City academy player who leaves the home team’s defence standing as he equalises.

Nelson's Sefton Gonzales celebrates scoring the winner with a back-flip

The victory for the hosts set up a meeting with eighth-tier Witton Albion in the next round of the competition

The club have spent £52,000 on new dressing rooms

A compelling game of combative and technically proficient football evolves on the Little Wembley baize, and it morphs into a question of which of the two outstanding goalscoring threats - Gonzales or Berry – will ultimately prevail. Berry spins and scores again after Luke Hepple has sent Nelson 2-1 up, but it is Gonzales who controls in close space and fires Nelson’s winner before sending his 6ft 2in frame through an improbable backflip.

The 3-2 scoreline blinks out from the new digital screen where they’re proud to display an image of the FA Cup and 87-year-old Eric Manning, whose meticulous, handwritten reports of the team’s games are typed up and published in the weekly Nelson Leader, can start reflecting on history repeating itself.

Next up, in the Preliminary Round, Nelson play eighth-tier Witton Albion, who they improbably beat on the way to a 3-2 loss at Port Vale in one of their most memorable Cup runs, in 1951. Manning missed the Port Vale game because his parents insisted on taking him on holiday.

Daily Mail Sport's Ian Herbert interviews Nelson manager Arron Ripley

We will be with Nelson at Witton, as the next in a series of pieces in which we take a club, any club, from the Preliminary Qualifying Round of the FA Cup, and follow them through the competition until they are defeated, then transferring allegiance to the victors…- and so on until Wembley.

The same project which Daily Mail football writer Brian James embarked on, exactly 50 years ago this month, for what became his legendary book, Journey to Wembley. We hope it will build a picture of the real football - our football – full of its hope, dreams, triumphs and setbacks.

Another of Nelson’s great historical claims is a 100% home record against Manchester United, given that they once beat them in the old Second Division and have never played them since.

‘We invited them over to play us and to see if we could extend that record,’ says Price. ’They’ve politely declined. We live in hope and they’d be so welcome!’ But a venture deep into the Cup would mean much more. ‘We want people to know what’s going on down here at our little place,’ Price says. ‘We believe that if we build, they will come.’

Sports.title: Premier League new managers ranked: The fearless Frenchman at Crystal Palace, Xabi Alonso's Chelsea revolution and a familiar face tipped to hit the ground running
Sports.content:
This season nine Premier League clubs have new permanent managers in charge, each with unique aspirations for the year ahead.

Europe’s most competitive league is not for the weak, however, as last season we saw managers crashing and burning in spectacular fashion.

This ranged from Ange Postecoglou’s 39-day stint at Nottingham Forest to Graham Potter’s disastrous spell at West Ham.

Daily Mail Sport have run the rule over the new bosses – who include some familiar faces – on the touchline and predict how well we expect them to fare.

Enzo Maresca (Manchester City)

Maresca is arguably the man facing the toughest challenge of the new bosses, as can anyone really replace Pep Guardiola?

We have seen managers before struggle to replace legendary figures at clubs, with recent examples including David Moyes following Sir Alex Ferguson at Man United and Unai Emery succeeding Arsene Wenger at Arsenal.

Moyes and Emery have both shown their capabilities before and after their respective spells at Man United and Arsenal, but it just did not work out for them at those clubs.

Maresca will be hoping to avoid a similar fate at Man City, as he follows a man that led the club to six Premier League titles, the Champions League and multiple FA and League Cups.

It might well benefit Maresca that Man City were not crowned champions last season, while he has had time to prepare after being approached midway through last season, contributing to his abrupt exit from Chelsea.

Maresca also worked at Man City under Guardiola so there is still some familiarity there.

Confidence rating: 7/10

Enzo Maresca faces the tough challenge of following the legendary Pep Guardiola at Man City

Andoni Iraola (Liverpool)

The former Bournemouth manager joined the Reds after the sacking of Arne Slot and will be hoping to bring his high pressing and unpredictable tactics to Anfield.

The Basque native left his mark at Bournemouth, leading them to their joint-highest league finish, highest point tally and European football in his final season at the club.

Liverpool fans seem optimistic about Iraola and the front-footed football that he promises, but their patience is finite, as evidenced by Slot’s dismissal.

He will need to get off to a strong start and there are concerns over the defence - further highlighted by shaky pre-season form.

Iraola must provide substance to go with the swashbuckling style or the pressure will mount.

Confidence rating: 6/10

Andoni Iraola enjoyed success with Bournemouth and will hope to make the step up at Liverpool

Marco Rose (Bournemouth)

Marco Rose, the man tasked with replacing Iraola, has had a volatile coaching career thus far.

His most high-profile spells came at Borussia Dortmund, where he lasted for just one season as the club failed to make it out of the Champions League group stage.

At RB Leipzig he won the German League Cup but was fired two seasons later after disappointing results in the Bundesliga and Champions League.

His experience of developing young players, however, should suit Bournemouth's recruitment strategy well.

Confidence rating: 4/10

Marco Rose was confirmed as Bournemouth boss in April and has had time to prepare for the Premier League

Xabi Alonso ( Chelsea)

Alonso enjoyed a highly successful spell at Bayer Leverkusen, remembered fondly for the 2024 season where he led the German club to their first Bundesliga title as part of a domestic double.

Leverkusen completed a full unbeaten Bundesliga season, breaking the European record with 51 matches without defeat, making Alonso Europe's most in-demand young coach.

The glaring blip on his resume is his stint at Real Madrid last season, where he was fired after a slow start to the season and in-fighting with some of the club's top stars.

The Spaniard inherits a similar version of organised chaos in west London, where he will have 46 senior players at his disposal.

The hope will be that his experience playing and leading at the highest level will help bring the glory days back to Stamford Bridge, with a more balanced dressing room, it would be no surprise to see Chelsea compete for at least a domestic cup. There's so much talent at Stamford Bridge, the Blues might even be dark horses as title contenders.

Confidence rating: 6/10

Xabi Alonso will aim to bounce back from his short stint at Real Madrid and show at Chelsea why he is viewed as one of Europe's top young coaches

Alvaro Arbeloa (Fulham)

Another manager who struggled to impress at Real Madrid is new Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa.

The former Spanish international joined after Marco Silva’s impressive five-year spell at Craven Cottage came to an end.

Arbeloa’s first-team management experience is limited to his six months at Real Madrid, where he was unable to control the dressing room and secure silverware.

His ties to the club have helped him to bring Madrid duo Gonzalo Garcia and César Palacios with him to Fulham.

But there are significant doubts about his experience, combined with the high expectations set by Marco Silva. It is imperative Arbeloa hits the ground running. It would be no surprise at all to see Arbeloa winning - or losing depending on how you look at it - the sack race.

Confidence rating: 3/10

Alvaro Arbeloa struggled at Real Madrid and has big shoes to fill after Marco Silva's successful stint

Matthias Jaissle (Newcastle United)

Jaissle enjoyed a hugely successful spell at Austrian club Red Bull Salzburg, where he won the domestic double and led the club to the Champions League knockout stages. After three years, he joined Saudi Arabian outfit Al-Ahli where he won consecutive AFC Champions League titles.

Unfortunately for Jaissle, his Newcastle squad is a shell of what it was even at the end of last season following the departures of Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon. Jaissle will be hoping that youngsters Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure can help ignite his new era.

The 38-year-old is unproven in major European leagues and despite his pedigree, without a serious recruitment drive, it feels as though he's swimming against the tide.

Confidence rating: 5/10

Matthias Jaissle will have to reshape a new-look Newcastle side after a summer of departures

Pierre Sage (Crystal Palace)

Sage joined after just one season with Ligue 1’s Lens, where he led them to the French Cup and a second-place finish, securing Champions League football.

This impressive record will be sure to excite Palace fans; however, his record lacks the sample size of other managers.

Sage, fresh off his French success, will be hoping his unfazed demeanour and fearless coaching will win over Selhurst Park faithful.

Confidence rating: 6/10

Pierre Sage impressed as manager of Lens last season and will look to adapt to the Premier League

Oliver Glasner (Nottingham Forest)

Glasner was won over by owner Evangelos Marinakis’s ambition and direction after calling time on a memorable stint with Crystal Palace.

The Austrian, a manager known for his impressive tactical knowledge, will be hoping that he can bring his deadly counter-attacking football to the City Ground.

The Forest job could be seen as a poisoned chalice but Glasner would have had his pick of attractive jobs across Europe and is a coup for the Tricky Trees.

Could he be the man to truly awaken the sleeping giant and elevate them even higher than Nuno Espirito Santo did or will the relationship with Marinakis wear thin as it has for a host of bosses?

Confidence rating: 8/10

Oliver Glasner surprised many by moving from Crystal Palace to Nottingham Forest this summer

Gary O'Neil faces the task of attempting to keep newly promoted Ipswich in the top flight

Gary O’Neil (Ipswich)

O’Neil replaced Kieran McKenna, who unexpectedly stepped down after leading the club back to the Premier League.

The Englishman’s last Premier League stint ended in December 2024, when he was sacked by Wolves with his side four points from safety and plagued with discipline problems.

It would be remiss to overlook, though, O’Neil’s spell with Bournemouth, where he guided them to a six-game unbeaten run in the 2022-23 season to keep the Cherries in the Premier League.

If O'Neil manages to steer the Tractor Boys to survival, he'd be in the running for manager of the season.

Confidence rating: 3/10

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
