World.title: Armenian Catholicos Garegin II attends first hearing in criminal trial
World.content:
Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

A court in Armenia‘s Armavir region has begun hearing the criminal case against the Catholicos of All Armenians and six bishops who serve on the Supreme Spiritual Council. Garegin II attended the hearing in person.

Clergy members and politicians gathered outside the courthouse. Lawmakers from the opposition Armenia Alliance and I Have Honour Alliance left parliament during the afternoon and travelled to Etchmiadzin to show their support for the Catholicos. Dozens of worshippers also gathered outside, periodically chanting “Your Holiness” and singing traditional Armenian church hymns (sharakans).

Prosecutors accuse the Catholicos and the senior clergy of obstructing the enforcement of a court ruling.

Garegin II removed Bishop Gevorg Saroyan, head of the Masyatsotn Diocese, from his post. Saroyan is one of the senior clerics who joined Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s campaign to “reform the Church”. The bishop challenged his dismissal in court. The court ordered his temporary reinstatement as head of the diocese until it reaches a final decision in the case. However, before the court could rule on the merits, the Supreme Spiritual Council, led by the Catholicos, also defrocked him. The council argued that the courts have no jurisdiction over the Church’s internal affairs.

Lawyer Ara Zohrabyan says the Catholicos faces criminal prosecution for carrying out his “ecclesiastical and canonical duties”.

He argues that state interference in the Catholicos’s decisions violates the principle of Church autonomy, the constitutional relationship between the state and the Church, and freedom of religion.

“In this criminal case, the court will examine not only the charges against specific individuals, but also another fundamental question: whether the secular authorities can interfere in the internal life of the Church and criminalise the exercise of the canonical authority of the Catholicos of All Armenians,” the lawyer said.

The trial comes after tensions between the government and the Church steadily escalated.

About a year ago, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan called for the Catholicos to step down. He first argued that Garegin II could not lead the Church because he had broken his vow of celibacy and had a daughter. He later accused the Catholicos of having links to foreign intelligence services. The ruling Civil Contract party has also included the removal of the “de facto head of the Church” in its election manifesto.

Members of the ruling party accuse the Church of interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy. The parliamentary opposition rejects that claim. Opposition lawmakers argue that it is the government that is unlawfully interfering in the Church’s affairs.

First hearing ends after 30 minutes as judge recuses himself

Shortly after the hearing began, Judge Hakob Manukyan announced that part of the proceedings would take place behind closed doors because they would involve “personal information”. He said the information concerned both himself and the Catholicos’s lawyer.

“A few minutes later, lawyer Ara Zohrabyan told journalists: “The judge has recused himself. He has withdrawn from hearing this case.”

According to Zohrabyan, the judge said he had once granted him his licence to practise law, which could “raise doubts about his impartiality”. Zohrabyan said he did not believe this constituted valid grounds for recusal.

“However, he refused to take part in this disgraceful trial. The very fact that the Catholicos is standing trial is deeply troubling. The case will now go to another judge.”

After the hearing, the Catholicos of All Armenians and his supporters headed to the cathedral to attend a church service and pray together.

Garegin II: “The authorities are trying to bring the Church under their control”

After the service, the Catholicos addressed those gathered outside the cathedral. He said the authorities were taking steps to undermine the Church’s authority, restrict its autonomy and bring it under their control.

“The authorities are persecuting the Church and the clergy. They have arrested and restricted the freedom of a number of clergymen, benefactors and other patriotic individuals through unlawful and fabricated criminal cases,” he said.

The Catholicos dismissed the charges against himself and the six clergymen as groundless.

“We remain steadfast in our faith and determination to defend our rights, which are guaranteed both by our country’s Constitution and by the fundamental principles of international law.”

Opposition declares a “day of shame”

Marianna Gakhramanyan, an MP from the opposition I Have Honour Alliance, said:

“Today is a day of shame. The Catholicos of All Armenians, our spiritual father and the head of our Church, is standing trial in Etchmiadzin. It is shameful and unprecedented. This is an attack not only on the independence of the Armenian Apostolic Church but also on Armenia’s Constitution, which clearly states that the political authorities have no right to interfere in the affairs of the Church and that the Church is separate from the state.”

“Who is defending the Church – us or you?” asks ruling party MP

Commenting on opposition lawmakers who came to support the Catholicos, Civil Contract MP Artur Hovhannisyan said:

“The Church has begun interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy.”

He also referred to the allegations that the Catholicos had violated his vow of celibacy:

“We are the ones standing with the Church. We are the ones defending the Church. You are defending clergymen who broke their vow of celibacy, who engage in politics and use religion and the Church to protect themselves from the consequences of breaking that vow and taking part in politics. Anyone who has broken the vow of celibacy should leave the Church.”

The ruling Civil Contract party’s election manifesto also outlines plans to reform the Church. Under the proposal, the “de facto head of the Church”, as Pashinyan’s team refers to the Catholicos, should leave office. The plan calls for the election of a locum tenens, the adoption of a new Church charter containing “mechanisms to preserve centuries-old traditions”, and, ultimately, the election of a new Catholicos.

Comment

Political analyst Tigran Grigoryan told Reuters:

“Pashinyan has come to see the Church as a political threat and as an institution capable of supporting the opposition and various political parties in their efforts to gain power.

“The case against the clergy fits into a broader pattern of selective justice pursued by Pashinyan’s government, under which leading opposition figures have been arrested and some of their property has been confiscated by the state.”

Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

World.title: Azerbaijan FM in Kyiv: gas for Ukraine, visit to Irpin, Ukrainian drones
World.content:
Azerbaijani FM visits Ukraine

Azerbaijan‘s Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov paid an official visit to Ukraine on 6 August.

It was the first visit by an Azerbaijani foreign minister to Kyiv since the start of Russia‘s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Bayramov began his visit with a trip to Irpin, where he viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones and laid a wreath at a memorial to fallen defenders at Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry.

He also held meetings with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, President Volodymyr Zelensky, Head of the Presidential Office Andriy Yermak, Defence Intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov and National Security and Defence Council Secretary Ihor Klymenko.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

One of the most notable announcements was Azerbaijan’s stated willingness to supply Ukraine with natural gas if needed.

The two sides also discussed the possible use of Ukraine’s underground gas storage facilities to strengthen regional energy security.

These developments are significant both regionally and internationally, particularly in the context of Azerbaijan’s relations with Russia.

In mid-July, Bayramov met Sergei Lavrov in Moscow and said the “difficult period” in bilateral relations was over and that ties had been fully normalised. A few weeks later, in Kyiv, he reaffirmed Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, while also signalling Baku’s interest in expanding energy cooperation.

The visit illustrates Baku’s multi-vector foreign policy. While maintaining dialogue with Russia, Azerbaijan has continued to provide humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and has expressed its readiness to support the country in the energy sector if required.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

Symbolic and practical significance of the Irpin visit

Irpin was one of the towns where the Russian advance on Kyiv was halted in 2022. Hundreds of civilians were killed during the fighting, and more than 70% of the town’s housing stock was destroyed.

Azerbaijan has contributed to Irpin’s reconstruction.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

The minister laid flowers at the bust of academician Zarifa Aliyeva in the park named after her, and visited the Zarifa Aliyeva Linguistic Lyceum and Irpin Central City Polyclinic, both rebuilt with Azerbaijan’s support. He was also briefed on future reconstruction projects, including plans to restore the town’s House of Culture.

In his statement, Zelensky said Bayramov had visited a school, a hospital and a rehabilitation centre supported by Azerbaijan. The visit to Irpin was seen as a demonstration of humanitarian solidarity with Ukraine, as well as Azerbaijan’s willingness to share its experience in rebuilding territories recovered from occupation.

I received Azerbaijan’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, @Bayramov_Jeyhun. This is the Minister’s first visit to Ukraine since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion. He began his visit in Irpin, where he visited a school, a hospital, and a rehabilitation center supported by… pic.twitter.com/7HTLIaz3EF — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) August 6, 2026

The visit to a town devastated by Russian forces, together with Bayramov’s review of reconstruction efforts and Azerbaijan’s continued support, was seen as underscoring Baku’s intention to reaffirm its longstanding position despite the “normalisation” of relations with Moscow, particularly its commitment to the principle of territorial integrity.

Following the official welcoming ceremony at the Foreign Ministry, Bayramov and Sybiha viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones. They then laid a wreath at the Memorial to the Fallen Defenders of Ukraine and observed a moment of silence in their honour.

Meetings and gas supply pledge

During expanded talks with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, the two sides discussed their strategic partnership, trade, energy, transport, humanitarian cooperation and regional security. Bayramov reiterated the need for an early end to the fighting and a diplomatic settlement based on international law, while reaffirming Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders.

He said Azerbaijan’s total humanitarian assistance to Ukraine had exceeded 50 million US dollars. Bayramov also highlighted reconstruction projects in Irpin and rehabilitation programmes for children.

During his meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky, the discussions focused on Russian attacks, the situation in the Black Sea, the disruption of grain export routes, defence cooperation, and cooperation in the energy, oil and gas, and agricultural sectors.

Zelensky thanked Azerbaijan for its energy and humanitarian assistance, as well as for maintaining constructive dialogue. Bayramov, in turn, spoke about the post-conflict situation in the South Caucasus and reconstruction efforts in the territories regained by Azerbaijan.

As part of his official visit to Ukraine 🇺🇦, FM of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 @Bayramov_Jeyhun visited the Embassy of Azerbaijan in Kyiv.



The Minister met with the Embassy staff and received a comprehensive briefing on the Mission’s activities. pic.twitter.com/UPqN5Hn9rx — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

At a joint press conference, particular attention was drawn to Bayramov’s remarks on possible gas supplies: “If the need arises, we will be ready to supply gas to our friendly Ukraine.”

He highlighted SOCAR’s long-standing presence on the Ukrainian market, as well as the importance of Ukraine’s underground gas storage system – the largest in Europe – for regional energy security.

The statement can be seen as signalling Azerbaijan’s willingness to contribute to the diversification of Ukraine’s energy supplies, while also supporting alternative routes for Caspian gas exports to Europe. Against the backdrop of Russia’s strikes on energy infrastructure in southern Ukraine, Baku’s offer also underscores the importance of competition and diversification in the energy sector.

During meetings with Kyrylo Budanov and Ihor Klymenko, the sides also discussed regional and international security, as well as prospects for energy cooperation. They reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of state sovereignty, territorial integrity and the inviolability of internationally recognised borders.

Expert: “Azerbaijan will continue to provide Ukraine with political, economic and humanitarian support”

lkhan Shahinoglu, head of the Atlas Research Centre and a political commentator considered close to the Azerbaijani authorities, wrote that the visit is being closely watched by Russia:

The Kremlin will closely monitor Jeyhun Bayramov’s meetings in Kyiv. Azerbaijan’s partnership with any country is an exclusive sovereign right, and no other state has the right to interfere in that process.

At the same time, Russia, which is waging a war of conquest against Ukraine, closely watches those who cooperate with Kyiv. President Ilham Aliyev‘s response to the same question from Ukrainian journalist Gordon, asked at the Shusha Global Media Forum two years in a row – that ‘Ukraine should not reconcile itself to occupation’ – angered chauvinistic circles in Russia. They believe Azerbaijan should accept the annexation of Crimea and the occupation of Ukrainian territories.

Just as Jeyhun Bayramov visited Moscow some time ago, he has now travelled to Kyiv. Ukraine is Azerbaijan’s partner, and Baku will continue to provide it with political, economic and humanitarian support.”

World.title: Giga Avaliani case: Two more arrested 10 months after Georgian teacher’s murder
World.content:
Two more arrested in Giga Avaliani murder case

Two more suspects have been identified in the high-profile murder case of a 28-year-old teacher in Georgia. On 5 August 2026, two teenage girls – Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili – were arrested.

Giga Avaliani, a mathematics teacher, was killed in October 2025. Five people have already been convicted over his murder, while the trial of a sixth defendant is still under way. With the arrest of the two girls, the total number of suspects in the case has risen to eight – all of them minors.

The arrests of Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili, after several convictions had already been secured, mark an unexpected and significant development in the Giga Avaliani case.

Nia Imnadze was one of Giga Avaliani’s former students and the girlfriend of the principal defendant, Aleksandre Gabashvili. Prosecutors accuse her of incitement to commit the crime.

According to local media, Anastasia Beruashvili is a friend of both Nia Imnadze and another convicted defendant, Giorgi Rikadze. She has been charged with failing to report the crime.

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics tutor, was returning home late on 1 October 2025 when he was attacked outside his apartment building. He fell into a coma following the assault and died on 24 October without regaining consciousness. Investigators say the attack was motivated by jealousy and what they describe as “unwanted communication with a girl”. The defendants have given a similar account. According to their version of events, Avaliani sent sexually explicit messages to his student Nia Imnadze, who told her boyfriend, prompting him to confront the teacher. Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, rejects that account. She says Nia had been skipping lessons and that Avaliani informed the girl’s mother, angering the student. According to Kupatadze, the attack was planned afterwards.

The Giga Avaliani case has become one of Georgia’s most high-profile criminal cases in recent years. Much of the public attention surrounding it has been driven by Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, who campaigned for what she said should be a thorough and impartial investigation. Her efforts also helped generate significant public pressure over the handling of the case.

From the outset, Kupatadze maintained that Nia Imnadze bore primary responsibility for what had happened and repeatedly called for her arrest. The recent detention of the two girls has therefore raised new questions.

But the key question remains: if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, why were the two girls not arrested earlier? Was their detention the result of new evidence, or did it come only after sustained public pressure and Eka Kupatadze’s campaign?

Detention of two girls

Both girls were arrested late on the night of 5 August, in what appeared to be coordinated operations. News of the arrests first emerged through a video of Nia Imnadze’s detention, which was released by her lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili.

The footage is deeply distressing. It shows a large number of police officers arriving at Nia’s home. Her mother, visibly distressed, pounds on the front door, shouting: “Come in, all of you!”, “Maniacs!”, “Murderers!”, “Do you know that Niako is innocent?!”

The girl’s father, meanwhile, tells the police: “You are going to make me do something the whole of Georgia will be talking about. If you treat my child so unjustly, I will do it.”

Police officers try to calm the distraught parents.

“Why are you taking my child? On what grounds? What does the court order say?!” the mother asks.

“The lawyer has reviewed the court order,” one of the officers replies.

“Giorgi, on what grounds are they arresting her?” the mother asks the lawyer.

“On the basis of a court order containing only formal wording, nothing specific,” the lawyer replies.

Nia sits in the hallway on a sofa, curled up with her face buried in her hands. The video is being filmed by her lawyer, who occasionally strokes her hair.

Shortly after the video was released, reports began circulating on social media that the second girl, Anastasia Beruashvili, had also been detained. No footage of her arrest was made public, but the Ministry of Internal Affairs later confirmed that she had been taken into custody.

During her arrest, Nia Imnadze became unwell and was taken to hospital, where she spent the night. On 6 August, she was transferred to a pre-trial detention centre. Anastasia Beruashvili was also taken there.

Minors charged in Giga Avaliani's murder case in Georgia – read more Five people have already been convicted in connection with Giga Avaliani’s murder: Aleksandre Gabashvili – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. He was the principal defendant in the case and was found guilty of organising a group assault and intentionally inflicting grievous bodily harm as part of a group, resulting in the victim’s death. Giorgi Rikadze – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. A friend of Aleksandre Gabashvili, he was convicted on the same charges. Demetere Chikovani – sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was convicted of attempted intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm in the Avaliani case, as well as organising group violence in connection with the case and four other incidents. Ani Naskidashvili – sentenced to five years and three months’ imprisonment. She was found guilty of failing to report a particularly serious crime. Another minor – sentenced to three years’ imprisonment. He was convicted of giving false testimony. The nature of the false statements has not been disclosed. His case was heard behind closed doors, lawyers involved in the proceedings are bound by a non-disclosure order, and the teenager’s parents have declined to speak to the media. According to TV Pirveli, the boy is named Luka Klatkin. Giorgi Malania – arrested in July 2026 and charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. Malania is the son of a former senior Interior Ministry official, who served as deputy interior minister between 2016 and 2019. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered.

Eka Kupatadze’s reaction

“Georgia has won another battle against the killers of a healthy, innocent and talented young man – Giga Avaliani!” Eka Kupatadze said in response to the girls’ arrests.

Giga Avaliani’s family has always maintained that those who carried out the attack were not the only people involved. They have consistently called on investigators to identify and prosecute all those who may have played a role in the crime.

The family has paid particular attention to the alleged role of the two girls. Eka Kupatadze has repeatedly said that they knew the attack was being planned.

Until recently, however, prosecutors had taken no apparent action against additional suspects, prompting repeated criticism of the investigation from Avaliani’s family.

Kupatadze even appealed for help to Ekaterine Khvedelidze, the wife of Bidzina Ivanishvili, the founder of the ruling party and widely regarded as Georgia’s “informal ruler”. Khvedelidze replied to her letter, expressing sympathy and support for the mother who had lost her son.

“As far as I am aware, the investigation has not yet been completed. I am confident that the relevant state authorities will see it through to the end and that all the circumstances will be thoroughly examined, so that no question surrounding the terrible tragedy that has befallen you remains unanswered,” Ekaterine Khvedelidze wrote in her reply.

Formal charges

On the evening of 6 August, both girls were formally charged.

Nia Imnadze at the time of her arrest

Nia Imnadze has been charged with incitement to intentionally inflict grievous bodily harm committed by a group. The offence carries a maximum sentence of 13 years’ imprisonment.

Anastasia Beruashvili has been charged with failing to report a particularly serious crime, an offence punishable by up to seven years’ imprisonment.

Under Georgian law, sentences imposed on minors are reduced by one quarter.

“The investigation conducted by the Ministry of Internal Affairs under the supervision of the Prosecutor’s Office established that, in September 2025, Nia Imnadze began taking mathematics lessons with Giga Avaliani. The accused, Nia Imnadze, told her friends Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Malania that her teacher, Giga Avaliani, had allegedly shown her excessive attention. By doing so, the accused incited Aleksandre Gabashvili to attack Giga Avaliani together with his accomplices,” the Prosecutor’s Office said in a statement.

According to the statement, Aleksandre Gabashvili, together with Giorgi Rikadze, Giorgi Malania and Demetere Chikovani, “decided to act on that incitement.”

What defence says

The defence has denied all the charges.

According to Nia Imnadze’s lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili, there is no evidence in the case to support the allegation that she incited the attack.

The lawyer also rejected reports that prosecutors had obtained data and messages from Meta, and that the arrests followed an examination of those materials.

“Criminal proceedings cannot be based on suspicion. They must be based on lawfully obtained evidence, and no other standard can override that principle,” Lekishvili told reporters.

Ketevan Vardanashvili, the lawyer representing Anastasia Beruashvili, made similar arguments. She said Anastasia had not witnessed any crime and that she and Nia Imnadze had seen each other only once, for a few minutes.

“They had no friendship and no contact,” the lawyer said.

As for Anastasia’s relationship with the convicted defendant Giorgi Rikadze, Vardanashvili said that “even if she was his girlfriend, that does not mean she had any knowledge of the crime.”

Complaint or incitement?

The arrests of the two girls have sparked intense debate on social media. Many commentators agree that everyone responsible for Giga Avaliani’s death should be held accountable and that justice should be served. Many have also expressed sympathy for Eka Kupatadze.

At the same time, some have questioned the actions of the law enforcement authorities. They have asked whether prosecutors have sufficiently strong evidence against the two girls, particularly Nia Imnadze, who faces a lengthy prison sentence if convicted.

The Prosecutor’s Office statement says only that Nia Imnadze told her friends that Giga Avaliani had allegedly shown her excessive attention. It does not explain whether she knew an attack was being planned or whether she urged her boyfriend to take any specific action.

“Does complaining to friends amount to incitement?” some social media users have asked.

Others have also questioned why, if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, the girls were arrested only 10 months after the murder. Some have asked whether the arrests were prompted by Eka Kupatadze’s campaign, and whether political influence may have played a role.

Those questions also remain unanswered.

Timeline of Giga Avaliani's case – read more 1 October 2025 – The attack

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics teacher, was attacked outside his home in Tbilisi. 24 October 2025 – Death

After spending 23 days in a coma, Giga Avaliani died. November–December 2025 – First arrests

Four minors were arrested: Aleksandre Gabashvili, Giorgi Rikadze, Demetere Chikovani and Ani Naskidashvili. April 2026 – First convictions

Tbilisi City Court found Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Rikadze guilty and sentenced each to 10 years and six months’ imprisonment. Demetere Chikovani was sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was later convicted over separate violent offences committed at a different time, increasing his total sentence to nine years and nine months. June 2026 – Another conviction

The court sentenced Ani Naskidashvili to five years and three months’ imprisonment for failing to report the crime. July 2026 – Another arrest

Giorgi Malania was arrested. According to prosecutors, he was charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered. August 2026 – Two more arrests

Two more minor girls were arrested: Nia Imnadze, Giga Avaliani’s former student and the girlfriend of the principal convicted defendant, and Anastasia Beruashvili, described as a friend of Nia Imnadze and the girlfriend of the second convicted defendant.

Broader picture

From the outset, the Giga Avaliani case came to represent more than a single criminal investigation.

It exposed a range of systemic problems, most notably a lack of public trust in investigative authorities. The case also highlighted shortcomings in Georgia’s juvenile justice system, as well as concerns over the protection of the rights of both victims and defendants.

Many observers questioned the release of footage showing Nia Imnadze’s arrest, particularly as it was made public by her lawyer. Some argued that the video was intended to generate public sympathy for his client.

“Unfortunately, public trust in the justice system – the police, the Prosecutor’s Office, the courts and other institutions – is now so low that victims, defendants and lawyers increasingly see shaping public opinion as the only way to obtain justice. They then seek to use public pressure to their advantage,” lawyer Londa Toloraia wrote.

In her view, this reflects a profound crisis affecting both citizens and the justice system itself.

“You no longer trust the state, even when it may actually be making a lawful decision.”

Toloraia also raised a number of questions about the arrests of the two girls: What evidence were they based on? Why did they take place 10 months after the murder? And why were they carried out at night, when Georgian law restricts procedural actions during nighttime hours, particularly in cases involving minors?

“How much influence does public opinion have over the justice system? A great deal. It is extremely difficult to withstand public pressure. And where institutions are fully politicised, it becomes virtually impossible to make a decision that is unpopular with the public,” she argued.

She stressed that legal standards must be upheld even when dealing with those accused of serious crimes – especially when the defendants are minors.

The Avaliani case has also exposed a darker side of public reaction. Following Nia Imnadze’s arrest, social media was flooded with hostile comments directed at both her and her family. Many users described her as the main culprit and called for severe punishment. Others went further, posting comments about the suffering they believed awaited her in prison.

A second group of social media users expressed concern about the tone of those comments. Toloraia addressed the debate in a lengthy social media post.

“Children are not born criminals. Before demanding that they be lynched, we should first ask why they became who they are,” she wrote, adding that juvenile crime in Georgia has reached one of its highest levels in recent years. She argued that the state’s response has focused on opening a “special prison” for children rather than preventing youth crime. A state in which parents who have lost a child must seek justice through public mobilisation, while institutions make decisions according to fluctuations in public pressure, is a broken state,” Toloraia concluded.

World.title: Odesa in summer 2026: Life between sea and war. VIDEO
World.content:
Beaches, bomb-damaged homes and explosions in broad daylight. In the summer of 2026, Odesa is caught between its traditional seaside resort atmosphere and the constant threat of Russian attacks. While some people relax by the sea and stroll through the city centre, others sift through the rubble left by the latest strike.

JAMnews visited Odesa to show what life in the city looks like today.

Odesa and the surrounding region remain frequent targets of Russian strikes. Residential neighbourhoods, critical infrastructure and port facilities have all come under attack.

Russia has carried out combined attacks using drones and missiles, seeking to overwhelm Ukraine‘s air defence systems.

The impact of these attacks is visible across the city. Residential buildings have been damaged, windows blown out and flats destroyed. Strikes have also hit Odesa’s historic centre, including heritage buildings and universities.

Ports in Odesa Region, along with the logistics hubs and warehouses that support them, are also regularly targeted. Attacks on port infrastructure have disrupted Ukraine’s transport network and Black Sea export routes.

The strikes often occur in broad daylight, when the streets are busy, cafés and shops are open, and beaches are filled with residents and visitors. At any moment, the familiar sounds of the city can be interrupted by explosions, air defence fire or the buzz of attack drones.

On several occasions, missiles have been intercepted directly over the coastline while beaches were crowded with people.

Today, it is possible to spend the day at the beach and the night in a bomb shelter.

World.title: “Russia’s annexation of Georgia’s regions would not go unanswered” – embassies on 18th anniversary of August war
World.content:
France, Germany, Italy, Britain: Russia’s annexation of Georgia

France, Germany, Italy and the UK issued a joint statement marking the 18th anniversary of the 2008 Russo-Georgian war, reaffirming their support for Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

18 years after the Russian aggression, we reaffirm our full support to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Georgia within its internationally recognized borders. We welcome Republic of Naoero’s decision to withdraw its recognition of the so-called independence of Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

We urge states that have established diplomatic relations with these entities to follow this example,” the statement said.

August 7, 2026 marks 18 years since the start of the Russo-Georgian war over South Ossetia. In the 2008 war, 412 Georgian military personnel and civilians were killed, along with 365 people on the Ossetian side. Some 20,000 ethnic Georgians were displaced. Georgia also lost control of 125 more villages in the Tskhinvali region (South Ossetia).

The independence of South Ossetia and Abkhazia is recognized by Russia, Nicaragua, Venezuela and Syria.

August 7, 2026 marks 18 years since the start of the Russo-Georgian war over South Ossetia. In the 2008 war, 412 Georgian military personnel and civilians were killed, along with 365 people on the Ossetian side. Some 20,000 ethnic Georgians were displaced. Georgia also lost control of 125 more villages in the Tskhinvali region (South Ossetia). The independence of South Ossetia and Abkhazia is recognized by Russia, Nicaragua, Venezuela and Syria.

France, Germany, Italy and the UK condemned Russia’s military presence in Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

ЭWe reiterate our condemnation of Russia’s ongoing military presence in the occupied breakaway regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia in violation of international law as well as Russia’s obligations under the six-point agreement of 12 August 2008.

Russia’s ongoing militarization of Georgia’s occupied territories poses a serious threat to the security of Georgia and to regional and European stability,” France, Germany, Italy and the UK said.

The statement also referred to rulings by the European Court of Human Rights.

In October 2025, the court found Russia responsible for a number of violations in the occupied regions, including the use of excessive force, ill-treatment, unlawful detention and restrictions on movement between Georgian-controlled territory and areas occupied by Russia.

“We urge Russia to implement the rulings of the European Court of Human Rights relating to this situation and to fully fulfil the commitments it made on August 12 and September 8, 2008,” the statement said.

The four countries also expressed concern over recent developments in South Ossetia.

They said the so-called “Agreement on Deepening Alliance and Cooperation,” signed by Moscow and the de facto authorities in South Ossetia on May 9, 2026, further violates Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and is incompatible with international law.

“This is a clear violation of international law. This document, as well as the appointment of a Russian citizen to head the region raise concerns on a possible full-fledged annexation of the region, which would not go unanswered,” the statement said.

Support for the Geneva International Discussions, co-chaired by the EU, OSCE and UN, was reaffirmed.

They said it is the only format that allows the parties to work towards a peaceful resolution of the conflict.

The statement also stressed the importance of the EU Monitoring Mission in Georgia and said its work would continue to be supported in the future.

News in Georgia

World.title: NSW Police forced to reopen investigation into Sydney gay club drug raids
World.content:
Police have been forced to reopen a misconduct investigation over drug dog raids on several Sydney LGBTQIA+ venues after an initial probe cleared officers of wrongdoing, the ABC can reveal.

Club-goers were allegedly pushed against walls and forced to strip in public as police led sniffer dogs through venues on and near Oxford Street on June 13 in the middle of Pride Month.

Complaints by Sydney MP Alex Greenwich and Sydney Lord Mayor Clover Moore prompted an internal police review, which last month concluded "no further investigation was warranted".

"The assessment did not identify any evidence of misconduct, unlawful conduct, or breaches of NSW Police Force policy by the officers involved," professional standards manager Inspector Michael Butcher said in a letter.

Club-goers reported being shoved, pushed against walls, and forced to remove clothing in full public view. (ABC News: Jak Rowland)

In the correspondence to Mr Greenwich and Cr Moore, Inspector Butcher said police had reviewed body-worn video footage, CCTV footage, police records and witness accounts.

"The operation was conducted in accordance with applicable NSW Police Force policies and procedures," he said.

"As a result, no further action will be taken in relation to this matter."

But the police watchdog, the Law Enforcement Conduct Commission (LECC), has decided to pull rank and use its power to force a probe.

"The [LECC] has conducted its own assessment and disagrees with the NSW Police Force's decision not to investigate your complaint," LECC Commissioner Anina Johnson said in a letter last week. "The commission has invoked our statutory powers and directed the NSW Police Force to investigate the matter."

The incidents occurred in the middle of Pride Month. (ABC News: Jak Rowland)

The LECC would review the police investigation, Ms Johnson said, and consider whether any further action was needed.

Mr Greenwich told the ABC he welcomed the LECC's decision to overrule the police assessment and require a full investigation.

"The community raised serious concerns about what occurred on Oxford Street, and those concerns deserve proper, independent scrutiny," Mr Greenwich said.

"This investigation is an important step towards transparency, accountability and rebuilding trust between police and our community."

The NSW Police Force has been contacted for comment, while the LECC said it was unable to comment.

Mr Greewich has welcomed the LECC investigation, saying it is about transparency. (ABC News: Keana Naughton)

'Reducing risks to public safety'

In his letter, Inspector Butcher said the decision to target the Oxford Street entertainment precinct "formed part of broader strategies aimed at reducing risks to public safety associated with possession, supply and use of prohibited drugs".

He said deployments were informed by intelligence, emerging drug trends, overdoses and fatalities, patterns of drug and alcohol-related offending, and offending within and near licensed premises.

In the aftermath of the operation, police said 93 people were searched, 42 drug detections made, and one person charged with supply.

Police said 93 people were searched. (Supplied)

In their complaint to the LECC, Mr Greenwich and Cr Moore said they had been inundated with reports from locals, many of whom were out celebrating Pride Month.

"Large groups of between six and 12 officers with drug detection dogs descended on the precinct, saturating venues and intimidating people trying to enjoy their night," they said in a letter.

" Constituents tell us that police pushed, shoved and aggressively directed patrons to move, shining bright flashlights in their faces, sometimes laughing and appearing to enjoy themselves. "

78er Rebbell Barnes, who witnessed a raid at Kinselas, said it brought back memories of the first Mardi Gras parade, which ended in violence at the hands of police.

The raids sparked debate in state parliament, with Greens MLC Cate Faehrmann accusing the police of "killing Sydney's nightlife".

The furore also led to 78er and historian Garry Wotherspoon quitting the LGBTQIA+ Consultative Committee, which was set up to promote a better relationship between police and the rainbow community.

World.title: Cairns community light candles for crash victim Savannah Spence Paige
World.content:
A 25-year-old woman who was killed in a multi-vehicle crash, allegedly caused by a man driving a stolen car, has been remembered at a community vigil held in Cairns in Far North Queensland.

Savannah Spece Paige died when her car was hit on the Smithfield Bypass on Wednesday, August 5 by a ute allegedly stolen from Palm Cove minutes earlier.

The late Savannah Spence and her husband Lachie Paige. (Supplied)

Last night, dozens of people gathered at Fogarty Park in memory of Ms Spence Paige, a Kewarra Beach resident.

Community members have came together to light candles for Savannah Spence Paige. (ABC Far North: Rosanne Maloney)

As the sun set, family and friends sat at the front of the crowd as candles were lit around a photo of the woman.

Shinae West organised the vigil after feeling the community needed to come together. (ABC Far North: Rosanne Maloney)

Vigil organiser Shinae West said she wanted to give the community a place to grieve together after the Ms Spence Paige's death.

"In honour of her life, and Cairns getting together and grieving together with the family, is really what it's about," Ms West said.

Family and friends showed support for the young woman's husband. (ABC Far North: Rosanne Maloney)

She said Ms Spence Paige's death "hit home" because her own family had experienced a similar tragedy almost two decades ago.

"My brother was killed in a car accident in 2007. It could've been avoided really," Ms West said.

A large crowd gathered on the oval for the vigil in Ms Spence Paige's memory. (ABC Far North: Rosanne Maloney)

Jake Edward Warn, 36, has been charged with manslaughter and four other offences over the crash.

He remains in custody ahead of his next hearing in October.

But police prosecutors have flagged they may ask for the charge to be upgraded to murder.

Ms Spence Paige's husband Lachlan attended the vigil alongside other family and friends. (ABC Far North: Rosanne Maloney)

Grief and anger

In the days after the crash, police described Ms Spence Paige's death as devastating for the whole community.

The crash happened on a newer section of the Captain Cook Highway. (ABC News: Conor Byrne)

In a statement, her family has since thanked locals for the outpouring of support, saying they were touched by plans for the vigil.

They described Ms Spence Paige as someone with an incredible sense of humour and a kind and caring heart.

"She has left a hole in our hearts that can never be filled," they said.

Forensic marks remained on the northbound lane of the Smithfield Bypass the day following the fatal multiple-vehicle crash. (ABC News: Conor Byrne)

The statement said she had only recently started a new life with her husband in Cairns.

Jenna Shingles said the crash had shaken her, and she attended to show support for the family.

"Our daughter is 17, and driving, and she just drove [the Smithfield Bypass] to have lunch with me half an hour beforehand," she said.

"It could have been anyone."

The road and verge of the Smithfield Bypass are still littered with debris following the fatal crash. (ABC News: Conor Byrne)

Alicia Clark said the crash was "close to our hearts".

"The whole situation is so tragic and to think it could have been avoided, it could have been prevented," she said.

Leonie and Mark Bowen say they came down to support the family. (ABC Far North: Rosanne Maloney)

Leonie Bowen said she felt compelled to attend the vigil.

"I think there's a lot of people here that are just here to say we care — there's not ... much else we can say," she said.

"Just to let the husband and the family know that the whole Cairns community is supporting them.

"They're not alone. It's so very sad."

Savannah Spence Paige and her husband Lachlan lived in the Cairns northern beaches. (ABC News: Conor Byrne)

An online fundraising attempt set up since the crash has so far raised more than $60,000, from hundreds of donors, toward helping Ms Spence Paige's husband Lachlan cover expenses.

World.title: Man arrested in North West Queensland after reports of shot fired at vehicle
World.content:
Police have arrested a man following reports of a shot fired in Kynuna in North West Queensland last night.

At 7:50pm, police were called to the Landsborough Highway to reports a shot had been fired at a passing vehicle.

Prior to police arrival, a motorist located a stationary Toyota Hilux in the centre of the highway and a firearm.

The motorist collected the firearm and continued on the highway to meet attending officers, where it was passed over.

Officers then attended the vehicle and located a 19-year-old man near the highway.

He was taken into custody and is assisting police with inquiries.

The Blue Heeler Hotel is the only pub in the town of Kynuna, with a population of 50 people. (Supplied: The Blue Heeler Hotel)

No-one was physically injured during the incident.

The owner of Blue Heeler Pub, Kynuna's only pub, who asked to remain anonymous, said the incident happened about 40 kilometres south of the township.

The town is 300km south of Mount Isa and has a population of just over 50 people.

Officers are appealing to anyone with relevant information or dash cam footage to contact police.

World.title: Aussie high jumper wins gold at under-20 world titles
World.content:
Australian high jumper Izobelle Louison-Roe has won gold at the World Athletics U20 Championships.

The 19-year-old came into the championships in Eugene, Oregon as the leading under-20 jumper this year, twice hitting a personal best of 1.95 metres.

She would not need a personal best to win gold on Sunday (local time), with a jump of 1.92m enough to be crowned champion, adding to the silver she won at Lima during the 2024 championships.

Hungary's Lilianna Bátori claimed silver and Spaniard Aitana Alonso won bronze, both jumping 1.90 metres.

"It was such an exciting competition, one of the moments of my life," Louison-Roe said.

"It was an incredible feeling when I won.

"I was crying so much I couldn't keep it together, it was amazing."

Louison-Roe was not the only Australian to medal on Sunday, with the 4x400m relay team securing a silver.

The Aussie quartet of Shari Hurdman, Xanthee Watts, Charlotte McAuliffe and Alice Hill ran a 3:31.39 to finish second behind the United States.

"Honestly, it's surreal to just go out there and get the job done," McAuliffe said post-race.

"I think we knew coming into this what we were all capable of, and we knew a medal was definitely possible.

" To go out and do the job is just amazing. "

Australia's men's 4x400m relay team — Seth Kennedy, Fred Hamblin, Dylan Hall and Chase Grant — came agonisingly close to also winning a medal, missing out on the podium by four-hundredths of a second.

Grant produced a brilliant final leg of 44.85 seconds, but was just pipped at the line by the French runner.

The women's 4x100m team — Thewbelle Philp, Zara Hagan, Grace Crowe and Emilia Reed — were also pipped at the line and placed fourth.

Kieran Shepherd ran a personal best of 3:42.25 to place eighth in the men's 1,500m, while Milla Roberts overcame a mid-race fall to be 14th in the women's 1,500m.

Elijah Wilson placed 13th in the men's discus final with a best throw of 56.47m.

World.title: The AFLW season opener was a double-header. Here's what fans thought
World.content:
As young Carlton star Poppy Scholz launched the ball into the stands at Docklands Stadium to kick the first goal of the 2026 AFLW season, fans were asking each other: "What do you think this crowd is?'"

The Blues were playing against St Kilda in the season opener in one of five double-headers between the men's and women's competitions this season.

Players, clubs and fans have been calling for regular double-headers to be introduced by the AFL to help grow the women's game.

This was in a bid to increase exposure of the women's game, try to adopt more fans across, give a unified club identity (one club, two teams approach) and allow the women to play on better conditions to allow for a better product.

St Kilda puts up a late challenge against Carlton but the Blues never give up their lead. (Getty: Morgan Hancock)

By half-time on Sunday evening there were 11,000 people in the crowd, 2,000 more than the sold-out Australia vs Ireland game at North Sydney Oval a week earlier.

Halfway through the final quarter, that number had ballooned to 20,455.

For St Kilda veteran and former captain Hannah Priest, they gave "a nice unity for an all-club approach".

"I look at the idea of all of your teams playing on the same day and celebrating each other," she told ABC Sport, acknowledging that a lot of club staff worked across both the men's and women's programs.

"To open the season at [Docklands] is a testament to every single AFLW supporter who has advocated for this sort of growth, and everyone who's been on board since the start. It's a celebration for all of us."

Blues' 26-point win over Saints Carlton has held off a St Kilda fightback to claim the opening win of the new AFLW season by 26 points in an entertaining game that made a case for more double header fixtures.

Across the stadium and fan sections, fans enjoyed the pizzazz of the bigger stadium, crowd noise and being sheltered from the rain.

However, there were also some who missed the community element of the suburban grounds and felt like AFLW was the main event.

Carlton AFLW fan Asha Ziffer, who has a membership for the women's team but not the men's, said she probably wouldn't have gone to the double-header had it not been the opener.

"I've got a lot of mixed feelings about it, but I don't think that this showcases it as it should be," Ziffer told ABC Sport.

"I think that it is presenting it as second to the men's game, and certainly for a season opener, W should be the focus."

There were 20,455 in the last quarter of the AFLW opener between St Kilda and Carlton. (Getty: Michael Willson/AFL Photos)

Ziffer said her 14-year-old daughter, Lily, said "it's like when you go to a concert and there's a support act that only half the people come to and then there's the main event".

"I think even if a 14-year-old can identify that, then it does say something more broadly to the community about where the women's game sits," Ziffer said, during the third quarter.

"Look, it's great and the game is going our way, which is great, even better. But it does feel, because it's such a big venue, I think 11,000 turnout is great but it just doesn't feel like a big crowd because the venue is so big. And you know, I'm sure it's a great ground for them to play on. And you know, it's nice to have a roof over our heads, given the weather's average."

Long time AFLW St Kilda fan Shae Williams said although her side didn't come away with the win, she hoped the team left the evening with a few more fans.

"It was exciting walking in and the thought of W starting … [although it] felt weird not being in a more intimate setting like Moorabbin.

"Twenty thousand attendance was a great result [and a] good experience for the players to play on a bigger stage," Williams told ABC Sport.

"The idea of double-headers are great, [although] I understand the need for W to have its own space as well."

Carlton won its opening match against St Kilda at Docklands. (Getty: Morgan Hancock)

Another Saints supporter, Dylan Cross, who got into both the games with his men's and women's membership, was pleased with the early turnout for the women's game.

"I heard a few people comment around me that haven't watched much women's footy that it was better than they expected," Cross told ABC Sport.

"So, hopefully it [double-headers] grow the game.

"I will say personally I still prefer the AFLW games at smaller grounds like Ikon or Moorabbin due to the more local footy vibes and that it's so family friendly. The crowd felt a bit reserved tonight.

"But all in all, I think it was a success and hopefully we see more double-headers in the future."

World.title: Australia's 'FIFO ghosts' a growing problem on census night
World.content:
As households across Australia begin filling out their forms for the 2026 Census, mining communities fear the count will fail to capture the nation's growing fly-in fly-out (FIFO) workforce.

The historic mining city of Kalgoorlie-Boulder, about 600 kilometres east of Perth, is experiencing one of the biggest booms in its history.

An aerial view of Kalgoorlie's Super Pit gold mine. (ABC Goldfields: Ivo Da Silva)

The rise in FIFO work practices has been so dramatic that Kalgoorlie-Boulder Airport is now among the busiest in regional WA, with more than half a million passenger movements.

Mayor Glenn Wilson has made regular use of the airport travelling to Canberra to lobby for changes to the Census while casting doubt on the accuracy of previous data.

"What we've continually done through lobbying of the ABS (Australian Bureau of Statistics) is to make sure our ghost populations are included," he said.

"We have got a baseline population, and then with the mining activities, those populations increase and put added strain on our infrastructure and our services."

He chairs the Australian Mining Cities Alliance which counts the City of Broken Hill, City of Karratha, Mount Isa City Council, Isaac Regional Council and the Shire of East Pilbara among its members.

Glenn Wilson is concerned "ghost populations" are not being included in the data. (ABC Goldfields: Jarrod Lucas)

FIFO boom at airport

When the first national census was held in 1911, the population of Kalgoorlie and Boulder, then separate towns, was estimated at a combined 19,605.

That grew to 29,306 as of the 2021 Census, with 20 per cent of the population employed in gold mining.

According to the latest ABS data, Kalgoorlie-Boulder's population was 31,268 at June 30 last year.

An aerial view of the Kalgoorlie CBD. (ABC Goldfields: Jarrod Lucas)

Mr Wilson estimates there could be as many as 10,000 FIFO workers in Kalgoorlie-Boulder due to the current boom.

"We know since the last census there's been more dwellings built in Kalgoorlie-Boulder, there are less rentals available, less houses for sale, so if this data comes back and tells us our population is going south, there is an issue with how the census is done," he said.

"Why is it important? Because funding opportunities at a state and federal level rely on up-to-date population figures.

"An increase in population gives us more opportunity to get more funding. It's as simple as that, because many of the grant mechanisms take your population into account."

Passengers line up for security screening at Kalgoorlie-Boulder Airport. (Supplied: Cass Be)

Kalgoorlie-Boulder Airport was built for 100,000 passenger movements a year back in the early 1990s.

City of Kalgoorlie-Boulder figures show there were 562,710 passenger movements in the 12 months to June 30, eclipsing the previous year's record of 458,876 passengers.

"Based on the airport figures, I am very optimistic we're going to see a population increase," Mr Wilson said.

FIFO workers on the tarmac at Karratha Airport. (ABC News: Cody Fenner)

Similar concerns in Pilbara

The FIFO workforce has been a long-term feature of the iron ore heartland of WA's Pilbara, where the 2021 census put the population at 82,000.

But Regional Development Australia's Pilbara chief executive Daiva Gillam said infrastructure was struggling to meet the needs of the local and FIFO population.

"I'm going to give you a real world example," she said.

"The Shire of East Pilbara in Newman are spending over $50 million of their own money to upgrade the wastewater treatment plant because it can't cope.

"For every person in Newman that lives there, there are up to three FIFOs all flushing the toilet in the East Pilbara.

"The infrastructure is not built to cope, but those workers aren't usually counted in the Pilbara as being residents."

Newman sits in WA's east Pilbara region. (ABC Pilbara: Charlie McLean)

Robert Powell is on a two and one roster, working two weeks in Port Hedland as a grounds person at a camp and spending the week off in Perth.

Despite spending more time up north, he will list his Perth home as his primary residence.

"Home is home, work is work, and it needs to be reflected that way in the census," he said.

"It's, to me, no different to saying I live in Armadale and work in Welshpool. It's where I live, it's where I want the services provided."

He suggested adding more questions to the census would help properly account for the FIFO workforce.

Workers leave a FIFO flight at Karratha Airport. (ABC News: Cody Fenner)

How are FIFO workers counted?

Census spokesperson Emily Walter said FIFO workers were similar to seasonal farm workers who can be a challenging demographic to collect data on.

She said the ABS had employed a dedicated team to coordinate with mine sites to enable workers to complete the census in the most accurate way.

"The census creates a snapshot at a point in time, like taking a photograph," she said.

"FIFO workers are often in a location for several days or weeks at a time, and the concept of a usual residence is one that we use to capture where someone is for more than six months of the year.

"If they are spending more than six months of the year at the location where they work, then they need to use that as their usual residence.

"That 'usual residence' concept is something that is really important for how we understand the data, and an internationally comparable definition."

A matter of 'belonging'

Organisational psychiatrist Cheryl Yam said the question ran deeper than data for affected FIFO workers.

"The question isn't simply 'where do I sleep most nights?' It's more where do I belong?" she said.

Cities like Kalgoorlie previously relied on a chiefly residential workforce, but the FIFO population is growing. (ABC News: Erin Parke)

"The camp really isn't necessarily home, but it's also more than just a workplace; because it's where they spend much of their day-to-day life."

Dr Yam said workers often felt the remote camp was where they stayed and home being where they lived.

Officials understand the sentiment, but say the workforce and infrastructure pressures across regional Australia meant every worker needed to be accurately counted.

In keeping with that growth theme, Ms Gillam said it was vital for regional areas that every worker was counted.

"Nobody wants to say that they live where they work," she said.

"But for the purpose of the census only, if you're here for six months, yeah, this is where you live."

The census data is scheduled to be released in June 2027.

World.title: Four more teens charged with Queensland man's murder
World.content:
Four more teenagers have been charged with murder after a 21-year-old died days after an alleged assault in Logan, south of Brisbane, late last month.

Eight people have now been charged with murdering the Redbank Plains man.

He was found unconscious with critical head injuries on Orchard Avenue at Bahrs Scrub by police on July 26 after reports of an out-of-control house party on Discovery Boulevard.

He was taken to hospital but died on August 1 from his injuries.

Four teenagers — three 18-year-olds and a 17-year-old — were arrested at Morayfield on Sunday and are due to face court today.

A total of nine people have now been charged in relation to the death.

On Thursday, three teenagers — Joshua Jackson John Jirima, 18, Amnaud Nduwayo, 19 and Kandour Khalil Tagelsir, 18 — were charged with murder.

A fourth — Sunday Obol, 19 — was charged with murder, intimidation, harassing or abuse, unlawful stalking, robbery, extortion, and deprivation of liberty.

A 22-year-old was charged with contravening an order to provide information necessary to access electronically stored information.

Police thanked the community for "significant cooperation" with the investigation, particularly "residents, community leaders and representatives who have worked with investigators and encouraged members of the community to come forward with information".

World.title: Three rescued from floodwaters after SA's weekend deluge
World.content:
Three people who drove through floodwaters have been rescued, following a weekend of heavy rainfall and storm activity across South Australia.

Several South Australian towns recorded record-breaking August rainfall totals across Saturday and yesterday, including 110 millimetres at Lenswood and 101mm at Coromandel East.

The State Emergency Service said it had received more than 530 requests for assistance during the weather event, mostly responding to flood-related incidents in the northern suburbs of Adelaide.

Meanwhile SA Police said three people have been rescued after driving into floodwaters at the intersection of Wingate and Winzor roads at Hillier.

Police said emergency services were called just after 4.50am on Monday, following reports that a car had driven into a flooded area.

Police said two occupants of the vehicle, a man and a woman, managed to get themselves out through the windows and safely to the side of the road.

While police were helping the two people, another car drove into the water and also became stuck.

The male driver was able to get out of the vehicle and was also helped by police to safety.

Both of the vehicles were washed away by the floodwaters, but police said there were no injuries as a result.

Senior Constable Daniel Isaacson told 891 ABC Adelaide the motorists made it safely to the roadside, but their cars are likely long gone.

"Both cars have since been washed away by the floodwaters and we reckon they're somewhere in the Gawler River," he said.

Commuters in Adelaide's northern suburbs were also disrupted this morning after the closure of Port Wakefield Road heading southbound, where the road meets the Salisbury Highway.

Motorists heading into the city have been advised to go elsewhere.

Fallen rocks have also closed Gorge Road at Paracombe between Corkscrew Road and Torrens Hill Road.

SA Police advised drivers to avoid the area.

World.title: Taylor demands PM apology for comment about Japanese ‘melons’
World.content:
Opposition Leader Angus Taylor has demanded Prime Minister Anthony Albanese apologise to his Japanese counterpart over comments he made about a “couple of melons” she gifted him, which he has denied was a sexual innuendo about the leader’s breasts. The attack on Albanese is the second time his appearance on comedian Nikki Osbourne’s Bush Deep podcast last month has faced the national spotlight, after the prime minister was forced to apologise for saying he wanted to “shag” pop-star Kylie Minogue on the same program. Loading Speaking at a Canberra press conference on Monday morning, Taylor said: “The comments were beneath the office of prime minister. They were insulting, and the prime minister should make a personal apology.” “The hypocrisy of Labor and the prime minister on this topic knows no bounds, no bounds whatsoever,” Taylor said.



During a visit to Australia earlier this year, Sanae Takaichi gifted Albanese a pair of “crown melons”, a gift often reserved for special occasions and offered as a mark of respect. In the subsequent podcast appearance, the prime minister at one point held his hands out in what many have interpreted as a gesture representing large breasts. Osbourne joked during the interaction that Takaichi had “smuggled” the melons into the country and was “looking like Pamela Anderson”. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese with Nikki Osborne on the Bush Deep podcast. “She brought two, as you do … and they are beautiful,” Albanese said during the appearance. A spokesperson for Albanese has denied the interaction was an innuendo.



During the same appearance, Albanese also suggested he scheduled sex with his wife, Jodie Haydon, after watching football, saying wins for his NRL team the South Sydney Rabbitohs were “always a good aphrodisiac”. Appearing alongside Taylor at Monday’s press conference was deputy leader Jane Hume, who said the comments were “grubby” and “inappropriate”. Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi and Anthony Albanese in May. Alex Ellinghausen “If you offend a woman, you should apologise to that woman. You should apologise personally, not in a statement. I think that the prime minister owes the prime minister of Japan a personal apology,” Hume said. “The fact that the prime minister has taken so long to make that apology, I think speaks volumes of the man’s character.”



Social Services Minister Tanya Plibersek, one of the most senior women in Albanese’s cabinet, backed the prime minister, arguing that the comments were being incorrectly interpreted. “I completely disagree with that interpretation of what the prime minister was saying … I think people can make their own minds, and they have,” Plibersek told Seven’s Sunrise on Monday morning. Related Article Opinion

Podcasts It’s possible for the PM to be casual and jocular – and also respect women Jacqueline Maley Columnist and senior journalist Appearing alongside the minister was One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce, who attempted to speak over Plibersek, and said Albanese’s remarks were “100 per cent wrong”. “That’s a really dangerous thing to say, Tanya … He’s an influence. You just got to be really careful ... It certainly has created a massive problem with one of our major partners, economic partners. I know in your heart, Tanya, you know it’s wrong, okay.”



Albanese and members of the Labor government have regularly spoken about the government’s pride in electing a majority female caucus, having gender parity in cabinet, and appointing women to high-ranking public service positions. The government has also campaigned at length on its partnerships in the Pacific, arguing that Labor under Albanese has restored respect to relationships with foreign partners following the tenure of the former Coalition government. World.title: ‘Gang war’: Suspected Irish crime kingpin charged after high-security Dubai extradition
World.content:
Updated WorldEuropeOrganised crime ‘Gang war’: Suspected Irish crime kingpin charged after high-security Dubai extradition Updated August 10, 2026 — 10:31am ,first published August 10, 2026 — 9:11am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

London: The alleged leader of an Irish organised crime gang was extradited to Ireland from Dubai to face allegations that he ran an international drug smuggling and money laundering empire with tentacles that stretched to Australia, Britain, Spain and the US. The Irish Air Corps plane carrying Daniel Kinahan, 49, landed at an airport on the outskirts of Dublin on Sunday evening (Ireland time) after courts in Dubai refused to block his extradition. Daniel Kinahan was detained by Dubai authorities in April on an Irish arrest warrant. Facebook Kinahan was taken to the Special Criminal Court in Dublin where he was charged with directing the activities of a criminal organisation. He appeared in the dock wearing a black hoodie and appeared calm, putting on a pair of dark-rimmed glasses and taking a sip of water from a bottle after taking his seat, London’s Telegraph reported.



Kinahan, who was not represented by a lawyer during the brief hearing, was ordered to remain in custody at the high-security Portlaoise Prison, about 145 kilometres southwest of the capital. His next court appearance is scheduled for October 5. Ireland’s Special Criminal Court handles all organised crime and terrorism cases, as well as others where prosecutors believe the ordinary courts are inadequate to ensure the “effective administration of justice”. Cases are heard by a panel of three judges without a jury. Kinahan, back right, leaving court in Dublin on Sunday. Alamy Stock Photo Kinahan fled Ireland in 2016 and had been living “an open and opulent lifestyle” in Dubai, the Telegraph reported. However, he was arrested after Ireland established an extradition treaty with the UAE. Irish media reported that a huge security operation was deployed in Dublin to ensure Kinahan faced justice. It included armed police, members of the armed forces and the prison service – which recently acquired a bombproof escort van to transport organised crime suspects, terrorists and other high-risk prisoners, Irish broadcaster RTE reported. The Telegraph reported the unprecedented security also included roof-top snipers and signal jammers.



The security precautions came after Kinahan’s family members were linked to a bloody gang war with another Irish organised crime group, the rival Hutch gang, that escalated after a failed attempt on his life at a boxing weigh-in in a Dublin hotel in early 2016. US authorities said in 2022 that the feud had resulted in 18 murders as they announced a reward of up to $US5 million ($7.1 million) for information leading to the disruption of the Kinahan organisation or the arrest and conviction of Daniel Kinahan. A reward poster issued US authorities in 2022. Alamy Stock Photo “Since February 2016, the [Kinahan Organised Crime Group] has been involved in a gang war with another group in Ireland and Spain, resulting in numerous murders, including of two innocent bystanders,” the US Treasury Department said when it sanctioned six members of the Kinahan gang and three businesses linked to it. US authorities also believe Kinahan has information on the export of Iranian and Russian crude oil using shadow-fleet tankers to China and India, and secret financial networks that Iran uses to finance Hezbollah and Hamas, the Telegraph reported.



Irish police, with the help of authorities in Britain, Spain and the US, have been pursuing members of the Kinahan gang since at least 2016, when the feud led to a daytime shooting during the weigh-in for a boxing match at a Dublin hotel. Kinahan was a boxing promoter at the time. The authorities allege the gang smuggled tens of millions of dollars in illegal drugs, including cocaine and cannabis, as well as guns into Europe, then used a network of apparently legitimate enterprises to launder the profits. An Irish government plane believed to be carrying Kinahan landing at Casement Aerodrome in Baldonnell – which is mostly used by the military – on Sunday. Alamy Stock Photo Loading Kinahan is believed to have run the day-to-day operations of the gang from his base in Dubai, the US Treasury said. That includes buying “large quantities of cocaine” from South America, organising its distribution in Ireland and attempting to smuggle drugs into the UK, Treasury said.



He has also instructed gang members to deliver money to a number of people in prison, including one who was convicted of attempting to murder someone on behalf of the organisation, the agency said. Related Article Exclusive

Organised crime Drug ring linked to Ireland's Kinahan cartel uncovered in Australia He was detained by Dubai authorities in April on an Irish arrest warrant. During a phone interview with Scottish podcaster James English last week, Kinahan denied being an organised crime boss and described himself as the victim of a conspiracy to tarnish his reputation. While he said the extradition proceedings were expedited due to a deal between the Irish and Dubai governments, he said he hoped his trial in Dublin would help clear his name.



“I believe, in a way, I am a scapegoat,” he said in the interview posted on TikTok. “And anyone that looks into this so-called feud that they say they have created, then you will see, you will see things yourself if someone has the time to look into it.” Kinahan has also spoken of his fear that he would be murdered in jail, the Telegraph reported. “If I happen to fall and bang my head when I have handcuffs on me, I didn’t fall. If I end up hanging myself, killing myself, poisoning myself, it didn’t happen. I’m not suicidal,” he said. In 2018, a drug ring linked to the Kinahan cartel was uncovered in Australia, with a two-year transnational investigation leading to the arrest of at least four Irish nationals here and in New Zealand. In March 2022, the head of the Kinahan organisation in Britain, Thomas “Bomber” Kavanagh, was sentenced to 21 years in prison after he was convicted of orchestrating drug shipments into the U.K. Two other men were sentenced to 20 years and 19½ years for their part in the crimes.



In the course of their investigation, police found 15 kilograms of cocaine and 220 kilograms of cannabis inside construction equipment fitted with a tracking device at the port of Dover on the English Channel, Britain’s National Crime Agency said when Kavanagh was sentenced. Kavanagh lived in a mansion equipped with bulletproof glass and reinforced doors in Tamworth, northeast of Birmingham. When police raided the property in 2019 they seized numerous weapons and £35,000 ($67,000) of cash in various currencies, including Emirati dirhams and euros, as well as British pounds, the crime agency said.
